The north is the feet, where the power of heat shines. Virabhadra is in the head, and he is iccha sakti, the power of will. That, he says, is what is meant by Virabhadra being in the south.

His map runs with the feet at the north and the head at the south. The line marked with an asterisk puts the world of Virabhadra at the crown of the andam, the cosmos (see note 16). As the head crowns the body, Virabhadra's world crowns the cosmos.

tamil: வேதாரணியத்தில் கதவு திறக்கப்பட்டதும் மூடப்பட்டதும் யாதெனில்: வேதப்பொருளை மறைத்ததுந் திறந்ததும் எனக் கொள்க. உண்மையை விளக்கியது திறந்தது, மறைத்தது மூடியது.
translation: What is meant by the door at Vedaranyam being opened and shut: take it as the meaning of the Vedas being hidden and opened. Making the truth plain was the opening. Hiding it was the shutting.
commentary: Vedaranyam, Thirumaraikkadu in Tamil, means the forest of the Vedas. Saiva tradition tells that the Vedas worshipped there and shut the temple door behind them, and that long after, Appar sang it open and Sambandar sang it shut again.

Vallalar gives the story one meaning. The door is the meaning of the Vedas. Opening it is the truth made plain, and shutting it is the truth hidden. It fits what he says of the scriptures in note 20, that their meaning was veiled and will come to light.

tamil: அப்பு தத்துவத்தின் குணம் நான்கில் இருந்துண்டானவையே நான்கு வேதமும்.
translation: The four Vedas all came from the four qualities of the water tattva.
commentary: One sentence, and it gives the Vedas a source inside creation. Appu, the water tattva, has four qualities, and from them the four Vedas came. He does not list the qualities here. Note 35 made Narayana the lord of the same water tattva. In this reading the Vedas, like the gods of the Puranas, belong among the tattvas, the constituents that the seeker learns to master and pass beyond (note 19).

sections.title: The Vedas, the Agamas and Other Scriptures

tamil: வேதம் பதி லக்ஷணத்தை விளக்கும். ஆகமம் பசு லக்ஷணத்தை விளக்கும். புராணம் பாச லக்ஷணத்தை விளக்கும். இதிகாசம் பத்தியை விளக்கும். ஸ்மிருதி கர்மத்தை விளக்கும். மேலும் வேதம் பதி பசு பாசத்தைச் சொல்லும். அதுபோல் ஆகமமும் சொல்லும். வேதம் என்பது நான்கு மகாவாக்கியந்தான். மற்றவை அங்க உபாங்கசாங்கப் பிரத்தியாங்கங்கள். இவைகள் யாவும் மனமடங்கும் துவாரமாம்.
translation: The Veda explains the nature of Pati. The Agama explains the nature of pasu. The Purana explains the nature of pasa. The Itihasa explains devotion. The Smriti explains rites. Further, the Veda speaks of Pati, pasu and pasa, and the Agama speaks of them too.
The Veda is only the four great sayings. The rest are its limbs, lesser limbs, attendant limbs and further limbs. All of these are doorways where the mind becomes still.
commentary: Five kinds of scripture, each with its own subject. Behind the list stands the Saiva triad of Pati, pasu and pasa. Pati is the Lord. Pasu, literally cattle, is the soul tied up like a tethered animal. Pasa is the rope, the bond of impurity that holds it (see note 26). The Veda explains the Lord, the Agama the soul, the Purana the bond. The Itihasas, the epics, teach devotion, and the Smritis, the law books, teach karma, rites and duties.

Then he narrows the Veda. It is only the four mahavakyas, the great sayings of the Upanishads, such as "That thou art". Everything else hangs from it as limbs, lesser limbs, attendant limbs and further limbs.

Last comes the measure he sets on all of them together. They are doorways where the mind becomes still. In note 20 he said the scriptures carry errors because their authors were touched by maya. Here he gives them their use. They help the mind to settle, and note 44 shows what lies beyond the door.

sections.title: The Ways of the Vedas and the Agamas

tamil: ஒருவன் ஆன்ம லாபம் பெறுவதற்கு இரண்டு மார்க்கம் உண்டு. ஒரு மார்க்கம் படியுள்ளது; ஒரு மார்க்கம் படியில்லாதது. எப்படி எனில்: மெத்தை ஏற வழியிருப்பதுபோல். ஏறிவிட்டால் மேலிடமாகிய அரமியம் ஒன்றே. அவ்வழி, ஆகமவழி சோபான முடையது. வேதவழி சோபானம் இல்லாதது. ஒருவன் ஆகமவழி செல்லாது வேத வழி போகக்கூடாது. ஏனெனில் ஜீவன் உபாசனா துவாரமாய் ஜீவத்துவங் கெட்ட இடத்தில், இரண்டற்று ஒன்றாகிய வேதவழி என்னும் அத்துவைதம் நிலைக்கும். வேதவழியான அத்துவைதம் அனுபவம்; ஆகமவழியான துவைதம் விவகாரம். ஒன்றென விவகரிப்பவரிடத்தில் அனுபவமில்லை. உபதேசரீதியில் சொல்லாது ஒன்றெனப்படவேண்டும்.
translation: There are two paths for a person to gain the benefit of the soul. One path has steps. One path has no steps. How so? It is like the ways of climbing to an upper floor: once one has climbed, the upper place, the terrace, is one. Of those ways, the way of the Agama has steps. The way of the Veda has no steps.

No one should go by the way of the Veda without going by the way of the Agama. For only where the jeeva, through the door of worship, has lost its jeeva-hood will the non-duality called the way of the Veda, where the two cease and become one, stand firm.

The non-duality of the way of the Veda is experience. The duality of the way of the Agama is practice. Those who argue that it is one have no experience. One must become one, without saying it in the manner of teaching.
commentary: Two staircases to one roof. Anma labham, the gain of the soul, can be reached by a way with steps or by a way without them. Vallalar's picture is a house with an upper terrace. However you climb, the terrace is one. The way of the Agama has sopanam, steps. The way of the Veda has none.

Its steps are upasana, worship. In worship the jeeva and God are still two, and that is dvaita, duality. The Veda speaks of advaita, non-duality, where the two end and only one remains. His order is firm. No one should take the Veda's way without first going the Agama's. Oneness stands only where the jeeva, through the door of worship, has already lost its jeevatvam, its separate jeeva-hood.

Then a pair of words. The non-duality of the Veda is anubhavam, experience. The duality of the Agama is vivakaram, the plane of practice and of everyday dealing. And a sharp line about talk. Those who argue that all is one have no experience of it. Oneness is something to become, without turning it into a lecture.
As practice the note is plain. Begin with worship and keep climbing. Let the sense of a separate self wear away on those steps before saying anything about oneness.
Two ways to the upper floor
1. The way of the Agama: it has steps. It is duality; it is practice.
2. The way of the Veda: it has no steps. It is non-duality; it is experience.
3. Once one has climbed, the terrace above is one.
No one should go by the way of the Veda without first going by the way of the Agama.

tamil: தேவாரம் என்பது: தேவ் - தயவு, ஆரம் - ஒழுங்கு, தயா ஒழுங்கே தேவாரம்.
translation: Thevaram means this: dev, compassion; aram, order. The order of compassion is Thevaram.
commentary: The Thevaram gathers the hymns of the great Saiva saints Sambandar, Appar and Sundarar. The name is usually explained as a garland for God. Vallalar splits it his own way. Dev is dayavu, compassion, and aram is ozhungu, order. Thevaram is the order of compassion.

Ozhungu is close kin to ozhukkam, discipline, the word in the title of his own Jeeva Karunya Ozhukkam. In note 19 he said the hymns were not sung by the saints whose names they bear. Here he reads the collection's very name as the steady discipline of compassion.

tamil: திருவாசகம் என்பது: மெய்ப்பொருள் நிரம்பிய வார்த்தை. மெய்ப்பொருளைத் தரும் வார்த்தை.
translation: Thiruvasagam means this: words filled with the true reality. Words that give the true reality.
commentary: The Thiruvasagam is the book of hymns that bears the name of Manikkavasagar. Thiru means sacred and vasagam a saying. Vallalar gives the title two readings, words filled with meypporul, the true reality, which is God, and words that give it. Note 48 calls it the best of all hymns of praise.

tamil: இந்த மார்க்க உண்மை தெரிய வேண்டுமாகில் திருமந்திரத்தைக் கவனிக்கில் விளங்கும்.
translation: If the truth of this path is to be known, it will become clear by attending to the Thirumandiram.
commentary: The Thirumandiram of Thirumular is a great work of Saiva doctrine and yoga, and Sanmarkkam is one of its own themes. Vallalar names it as the book that makes the truth of "this path" clear. Attend to it, he says, and the truth will show itself.

tamil: சாத்திரங்களிற் சிறந்தது திருமூலர் திருமந்திரம். இஃது மொத்தம் எண்ணாயிரம்; தோத்திரங்களிற் சிறந்தது திருவாசகம். இவற்றை ஊன்றிப் பார்க்கவும்.
translation: The best among the doctrinal works is Thirumular's Thirumandiram. It is eight thousand in all. The best among the hymns of praise is the Thiruvasagam. Look into these closely.
commentary: Two books, each first in its class. A sastra is a work of doctrine, and among those the Thirumandiram leads. A stotra is a hymn of praise, and there the Thiruvasagam leads. He puts the Thirumandiram at eight thousand. The text that has come down to us holds about three thousand verses, and the figure stands as printed. His instruction is to look into both closely, with slow and steady attention.

sections.title: The Meaning of the Word Sivam

tamil: சிவம் என்பதற்குப் பொருள் சச்சிதானந்தம். சச்சிதானந்த மென்பது சத்து, சித்து, ஆனந்தம். இதில் சிகரம் சத்து. வகரம் சித்து, மகரம் ஆனந்தம்; சிகரம் எல்லா முள்ளதாய் விளங்குவது, வகரம் எல்லாம் விளங்குவதா யுள்ளது, மகரம் இரண்டினாலும் நிரம்பிய வின்பம்.
translation: The meaning of Sivam is sachchidanandam. Sachchidanandam is being, knowledge and bliss. In this, the letter si is being, the letter va is knowledge, the letter m is bliss. Si is that which shines as all that is. Va is that which is as the shining of all. M is the bliss filled by both.
commentary: Sivam, the word Vallalar uses most often for God, is here unfolded as sat-chit-ananda. Sat is being, chit is knowledge or consciousness, ananda is bliss. He finds the three inside the Tamil word itself, which is written as three sounds, si, va and a closing m.

Si is being, that which shines as all that is. Va is knowledge, that which exists as the shining of everything. The closing m is bliss, filled by the other two. Being and knowing meet, and their meeting is joy. Read his way, the name already holds the whole of what it names.

tamil: சிவம் என்பதற்குப் பொருள் ஸச்சிதானந்தம். ஸச்சிதானந்த மென்பது ஸத்து சித்து ஆனந்தம். சி சத்து, வ சித்து, ம் ஆனந்தம். சி எல்லாம் உள்ளதாய் விளங்குவது, வ எல்லாம் விளங்குவதாயுள்ளது, ம் இந்த இரண்டினாலும் நிரம்பிய இன்பம்.
translation: The meaning of Sivam is sachchidanandam. Sachchidanandam is being, knowledge and bliss. Si is being, va is knowledge, m is bliss. Si is that which shines as all that is. Va is that which is as the shining of all. M is the bliss filled by these two.
commentary: These notes were written down by devotees who heard Vallalar teach, and the editor set each listener's shorter record after the main note. This one repeats the record above nearly word for word. The one small difference is that the bliss is filled "by these two", pointing back to being and knowledge.

tamil: சிவ என்பதற்குப் பொருள் அனாதியாய் மலமில்லாத சர்வ வல்லமை யுடையது. சி என்பதற்குப் பொருள் அனாதியாய் மலமில்லாதது; வ என்பதற்குப் பொருள் சர்வவல்லமை யுடையது.
translation: The meaning of Siva is: that which is without impurity from beginningless time and has all power. The meaning of si is: that which is without impurity from beginningless time. The meaning of va is: that which has all power.
commentary: Without its closing m, the word Siva yields two qualities. Si is freedom from mala, impurity, from anadi, beginningless time. Mala is the stain that binds souls, counted in Saiva teaching as three, anava, karma and maya. Beginningless means Siva was never stained and never had to be cleansed. Va is sarva vallamai, all power.

tamil: சிவ என்பதன் பொருள் அனாதியாய் மலமில்லாத சர்வ வல்லப முடையது. சி என்பது அனாதியாய் மலமில்லாதது, வ என்பது சர்வ வல்லப முடையது.

மேலும் சி என்னு மெழுத்துக்குப் பொருள் ஒருவாறு: இதிலடங்கிய பீஜம் 5. அவையாவன: தோன்றி அசைதலாகிய விந்து ஒன்று, அதன் புடைபெயர்ச்சி ஒலியாகிய நாதம் 2, அதன் வண்ண வடிவமாகிய வரி அக்கரத்தின் சகரமெய் யென்னும் ச் 3, அதனது குணங்களை வெளிப்படுத்தும் ஆதி அக்கரமாகிய பிரணவ மூல அகரம் 4, இதைத் தன் வண்ணச் சுபாவத்தோடு வெளியில் தோன்றச் செய்வித்து விளக்கும் அருட்பிரணவமாகிய இகரம் 5, ஆகக் கூடிய விந்துக்களைந்தும் ஓருருவமாய்ச் சிகரமாயிற்று. இதன் இலக்கணம் விரிக்கிற் பெருகும். அனுபவத்தா லறிக.
translation: The meaning of Siva is: that which is without impurity from beginningless time and has all might. Si is that which is without impurity from beginningless time. Va is that which has all might.

Further, the meaning of the letter si, in outline: the seeds contained in it are five. They are: bindu, which is appearing and stirring, one; nada, the sound of its shifting, 2; the consonant s of the written letter, which is its colored form, 3; the vowel a, the first letter, the root of the Pranava, which brings out its qualities, 4; the vowel i, the Pranava of grace, which makes it appear outside with its own colored nature and makes it shine, 5. These five seeds together became one form, the letter si. Its grammar, if unfolded, would grow long. Know it by experience.
commentary: The two qualities appear once more, and then he opens the single letter si. It holds five bija, seeds. Bindu, the seed-point of light, is the first stirring. Nada, the primal sound, is the sound of that stirring (both are met in note 1). Third comes the consonant itself as written, its visible shape. Fourth is the vowel a, which he calls the first letter and the root of the Pranava, the sacred syllable Om. Fifth is the vowel i, which he names arut pranavam, the Pranava of grace, because it brings the letter out with its own nature and makes it shine.

A little Tamil grammar helps here. A Tamil consonant is spoken with the vowel a built in, and si is that consonant with i in the place of a. So his five seeds hold both vowels, the hidden a as the root and the i as grace. The full account, he says, would run very long. Know it by experience.

tamil: சி என்னு மெழுத்துக்குப் பொருள்: இதன் பீஜாக்ஷரம் 5. அவையாவன: பிந்து, நாதம். சகரஒற்று, அகரம், இகரம். இவை கூடியது சிகரமாகிய ஓர் உருவம் இதற்குப் பொருள் சுத்த சன்மார்க்க காலத்தில் வெளிப்படும்.
translation: The meaning of the letter si: its seed-letters are five. They are bindu, nada, the consonant s, the vowel a and the vowel i. These together are one form, the letter si. Its meaning will come out in the time of Suddha Sanmarkkam.
commentary: The five seeds are listed again in brief. This time he gives no reading of them and makes a promise instead. The meaning of si will come out in the time of Suddha Sanmarkkam, the pure path of truth that he taught (see note 18).

sections.title: The Qualities of Siva and of the Jeeva

blocks.html: Eight Qualities of Siva, Eight Qualities of the Jeeva (சிவகுணம் 8 ஜீவகுணம் 8)

tamil: தன் வயத்தனாதல் பராதீனன்
தூய உடம்பினனாதல் துக்கதேகி
இயற்கை யுணர்வினனாதல் செயற்கை உணர்வினன்
முற்றும் உணர்தல் சிற்றுணர்வினன்
இயல்பாகவே பாசங்களினீங்குதல் பந்தன்
பேரருளுடைமை காடின்னியன்
முடிவிலாற்ற லுடைமை நிர்பவன்
வரம்பிலின்ப முடைமை மலதேகி
translation: Being self-dependent: one dependent on another
Having a pure body: one with a body of sorrow
Having knowledge by nature: one of acquired knowledge
Knowing all: one of little knowledge
Being free of bonds by nature: one who is bound
Having great grace: one who is hard-hearted
Having endless power: one without power
Having boundless bliss: one with a body of impurity
commentary: Eight against eight, read across the line. The left column gives the eight qualities of Siva. They are the eight that Parimelazhagar, the classic commentator on the Thirukkural, lists for the Kural's "Lord of eight qualities". Self-dependence, a pure body, knowledge by nature, knowing all, freedom from bonds by nature, great grace, endless power and boundless bliss.

Vallalar sets beside each one the state of the jeeva, the individual life. The self-dependent faces the dependent, and a pure body faces a body of sorrow. Natural knowledge faces knowledge gathered from outside, and the all-knowing faces the little-knowing. The free faces the bound, endless power faces no power, and boundless bliss faces a body of impurity.

One pair stands out for anyone who knows his teaching. Opposite perarul, great grace, he puts kadinyan, the hard-hearted. In this table the lack of grace in a person shows as a hard heart. Note 51 draws the same line from the other side.

tamil: பசுவென்பது முற்றும் மலமுள்ளது.
ஜீவனென்பது மூன்று பங்கு மலமுள்ளது.
ஆன்மாவென்பது ஒரு பங்கு மலமுள்ளது.
சிவம் முற்றும் மலம் நீங்கியது. ஆதலால் மலம் முற்றும் நீங்கித் தயா வடிவமாவதே சிவமாதல்.
translation: The pasu has impurity in full.
The jeeva has three parts impurity.
The soul has one part impurity.
Sivam is wholly free of impurity. Therefore, to be wholly freed of impurity and to become the form of compassion is becoming Sivam.
commentary: Three grades of the self, measured by mala, impurity (see note 49). The pasu, the soul tied like cattle (note 43), is impurity through and through. The jeeva, the individual life, carries three parts, and the anma, the soul, carries one. Note 1 set these layers one inside the other, and here each layer has its share of stain.

Sivam has none at all. From that Vallalar draws his definition of the goal. To be cleared of every impurity and to become daya vadivam, the very form of compassion, is to become Sivam. The clearing and the compassion are named together in one breath.

Few lines in the book put his teaching so briefly. Becoming God is described as becoming compassion. The note gives no method. Elsewhere his method is Jeevakarunyam, compassion shown to every living being, and this line shows where that compassion leads.
How much impurity each holds
Each bar is drawn in four parts; dark is impurity.
1. The pasu has impurity in full.
2. The jeeva has three parts impurity.
3. The soul has one part impurity.
4. Sivam is wholly free of impurity. To be wholly freed of impurity and to become the form of compassion is becoming Sivam.

tamil: சமய சூக்கும பஞ்சாக்கரத்தின் தாத்பரியம் நான்கு, மேற்படி அக்ஷரம் 5: சிவாயநம - இதற்குத் தாத்பரியம் நான்காவன. பூர்வம், பூர்வபூர்வம், உத்தரம், உத்தரோத்தரம் ஆக 4. இதில் பூர்வத்திற்கு அர்த்தம்: சிவனை நமஸ்கரிக்கின்றேன். பூர்வபூர்வத்திற்குத் தாத்பரியம்: அனாதியில் மலமில்லாது எல்லாமுடைய சிவத்திற்கு என்னுடைய கரண உள்ளங்களைச் சமர்ப்பிக்கின்றேன். மற்ற இரண்டிற்கும் அர்த்தம் அனுபவத்தால் தெரியலாம். இதுபோல் மத சன்மார்க்கத்திற்கும் மேற்படி அக்ஷரமே. அதற்கும் முன்போலவே நான்கு தாத்பரிய முள்ளது. அதில் பூர்வத்திற்குத் தாத்பரியம்: சி என்பது பதி, வா என்பது சத்தி, ய வென்பது ஜீவன், ந வென்பது திரோதை, ம வென்பது மாமாயை; ஆதலால், மாமாயை திரோதை நீங்கி, ஜீவ போத மற்று, அருள் வடிவாய்ச் சிவமாவது. பூர்வபூர்வத்தின் தாத்பரியம்: சி என்பது எல்லாமுடையது, வா என்பது அபிந்நமாகிய அருள், ய வென்பது ஆன்ம சிற்சபை, ந வென்பது சீவன், ம வென்பது பசு; ஆதலால் பசுத்தன்மை கெட்டு, ஜீவபோதம் போய், ஆன்ம வியற்கை வடிவாய்ச் சத்துவமயமாய் எல்லாமுடையதுவாய்ப் பூரணமாய் நிற்றல்; ஒருவாறு. அனுபவத்தில், பரவிந்து பரநாதம் பரத்திலும், அபரவிந்து அபரநாதம் பூர்வத்திலும் வழங்கும். இவ்வளவும் செபமூலமாய்க் கரண சுத்தி வந்து, அக்ஷர முன்னுதலை விட்டு, அறிவாகிருதியாய், கருணையும் சிவமுமே பொருளெனும்படி நிற்றற்கு முதற்றுவாரமாம். மற்ற உத்தரத்தில் ஏம சித்தியும் உத்தரோத்தரத்தில் தேகசித்தியும் சொல்லும். இஃது மத சன்மார்க்க அனுஷ்டானம். இதுபோல் சமயத்திலும் தேகசித்தியும் ஏமசித்தியு முள. மேற்குறித்த சமய மதங்களின் விரிவு அனந்தகோடி. அந்த சித்திகள் யாவும் அவ்வச்சமய மதங்களின் கர்த்தா மூர்த்தி தலைவன் தலைவி முதலியவர்கள் பதப்பிராப்தி வரையிலும் நிற்கும். ஆதலால் மேற்குறித்த இரண்டு சித்தியும் எக்காலத்தும் அழிவுறா திருப்பதாகச் சொல்லுவது சுத்த சன்மார்க்க பூர்வோத்தரம். ஏமசித்தி' தேகசித்தி ஆகிய இவற்றை மேற்குறித்த சூக்கும பஞ்சாக்கரத்தில் சொல்லுவதற்குப் பிரமாணம்:- "சிவாயநம வெனச் செம்பு பொன்னாயிடும்"” "சிவாயநமவெனச் சிந்தித்திருப்பார்க்கு அபாய மொருநாளு மில்லை." ஆதலால், மேற்குறித்த அக்கரத்தை மகான்கள் குழுக்குறியாக - வரிவடிவாய் - சுட்டினார்கள். இதை அக அனுபவிகள் தத்துவங்களை அறிந்து, அனுசந்தானஞ் செய்வார்கள். சாதகிகளுக்கு நாவினாலுன்னிக் கரண மோய்ந்தால், தத்துவானுசந்தானஞ் செய்யக்கூடும்.
1. ஏமசித்தி - பொன் செய்யும் வல்லபம்.
2. திருமந்திரம் 903
3. நல்வழி 15 (ஒளவையார்)
translation: The meanings of the subtle five-letter mantra of religion are four, and its letters are five: Si-va-ya-na-ma. Its four meanings are purvam, purva-purvam, uttaram and uttarottaram: 4. Of these, the meaning of the purvam is: I bow to Siva. The meaning of the purva-purvam is: I offer my inner faculties to Sivam, which from beginningless time is without impurity and has all. The meaning of the other two may be known by experience.

In the same way, for the Sanmarkkam of the creeds too the letters are the same, and it too has four meanings as before. The meaning of its purvam is: si is the Lord, va is Sakti, ya is the jeeva, na is the veiling power, ma is the great maya. Therefore: the great maya and the veiling go, the jeeva's sense of self ceases, and one becomes Sivam in the form of grace.

The meaning of the purva-purvam is: si is that which has all, va is grace, which is inseparable from it, ya is the soul, the Hall of Consciousness, na is the jeeva, ma is the pasu. Therefore: the pasu-nature perishes, the jeeva's sense of self goes, and one stands complete, in the form of the soul's own nature, made wholly of sattva, having all. That is it in outline. In experience, the para-bindu and para-nada are at work in the para, and the apara-bindu and apara-nada in the purva.

All this is the first doorway to standing thus: through repetition the faculties become pure, one leaves off dwelling on the letters, takes the form of knowledge, and stands so that compassion and Sivam alone are the reality. The uttaram speaks of hema siddhi, and the uttarottaram of deha siddhi. This is the practice of the Sanmarkkam of the creeds. In the same way, in religion too there are deha siddhi and hema siddhi.

The spread of the religions and creeds named above runs to countless millions. All those attainments stand until one reaches the station of the maker, the deity, the lord, the lady and the rest of each of those religions and creeds. Therefore, to speak of these two attainments as remaining undestroyed for all time is the first and the later meaning of Suddha Sanmarkkam.

The authority for saying that the subtle five-letter mantra named above speaks of hema siddhi and deha siddhi: "Say Sivayanama, and copper turns to gold." "For those who keep thinking Sivayanama, there is no danger on any day." Therefore the great ones pointed to these letters as a coded sign, in written form. Those of inner experience know the tattvas and contemplate it. For practitioners, if they dwell on it with the tongue and the faculties grow still, contemplation of the tattvas becomes possible.
1. Hema siddhi: the power to make gold.
2. Thirumandiram 903.
3. Nalvazhi 15 (Avvaiyar).
commentary: Sivayanama, the Panchakshara or five-letter mantra, is the best-known prayer of Saivism. Vallalar reads it on two levels. Samayam, religion, is the level of worship and observance. Matham, the creeds, are the schools of doctrine, and "the Sanmarkkam of the creeds" is his name for the path the mantra opens there. On each level it has four meanings, purvam, the first, purva-purvam, the first of the first, uttaram, the later, and uttarottaram, the later of the later.

In religion the first two are simple. I bow to Siva. I offer my inner faculties to Sivam, ever free of impurity, who has all. In the creeds the letters become a map of release. Si is the Lord and va is Sakti, His power. Ya is the jeeva. Na is tirodhai, the veiling power that hides the truth from the soul, and ma is mahamaya, the great maya. When maya and the veil go and the jeeva's sense of self ends, one becomes Sivam in the form of grace. The second reading runs from the bound pasu through the jeeva to the soul as the Hall of Consciousness, the Chit Sabhai.

Then the line to hold on to. All of this is a first doorway only. Repeating the mantra purifies the faculties, until one lets go of the letters, takes the form of knowledge, and stands where compassion and Sivam alone are real.

The later meanings speak of hema siddhi, the making of gold, and deha siddhi, the perfection of the body. Every religion and creed has them, he says, and they hold only until a person reaches the station of that faith's own god. His claim for Suddha Sanmarkkam is that these two attainments never perish. The proof-texts from the Thirumandiram and from Avvaiyar are kuzhuukkuri, coded speech (the three numbered lines are the editor's).
As practice, the note gives a ladder. Repeat the mantra with the tongue until the faculties grow quiet, and contemplation of the tattvas becomes possible.

tamil: உலகிகள் நாவினாலுன்னத் தங்கள் மனோரதம் சித்திக்கும். வகர வித்தை” யுடையவர்கள் மேற்படி அக்கரத்தின் உண்மையைப் பவுதிகம், லோகம், ஓஷதி, லவணம், முதலியவற்றிற் சேர்த்து வகரத்தை முடிப்பார்கள். தகர வித்தை” யுடையவர்கள் அதுபோலவே அமைத்துக்கொண்டு தேகத்தை நீடிக்கச் செய்வார்கள். ஆதலால் மேற்குறித்த அக்கரங்கள் பரிபாஷை. இதனது உண்மை யாவும் சுத்த சன்மார்க்க சகஜசாத்திய ஞானானுபவிக்கு விளங்கும்.
4. வகரவித்தை - பொன் செய்தல்.
5. தகரவித்தை - தேகசித்தி செய்துகொள்ளல்.
translation: Worldly people repeat it with the tongue, and their wishes are fulfilled. Those who have the vakara vidya join the truth of these letters to elemental substances, metals, herbs, salts and the like, and complete the va. Those who have the thakara vidya set it up in the same way and make the body last long. Therefore these letters are code language. All their truth will be clear to the one who has the experience of wisdom, natural and attainable, in Suddha Sanmarkkam.
4. Vakara vidya: making gold.
5. Thakara vidya: gaining the perfection of the body.
commentary: Three kinds of people use the same five letters. Worldly people repeat them with the tongue and get what they wish for. Those with vakara vidya, the art of va, join the letters' hidden truth to minerals, metals, herbs and salts and make gold. Those with thakara vidya, the art of tha, use them the same way to make the body last. The editor's two numbered lines say just this.

So the letters are paribhasha, code language, a vocabulary with a meaning hidden inside it. Their whole truth opens to one whose wisdom is sahaja, natural, and sadhya, within reach, in Suddha Sanmarkkam.

tamil: சமயத்தில் சிவாயநம வென்னும் வாக்கியத்திற்குத் தாத்பரியம் 4 வகைப்படும்: பூர்வம், பூர்வபூர்வம், உத்தரம், உத்தரோத்தரம். பூர்வம்: சிவனை நமஸ்கரிக்கின்றேன் என்பது. பூர்வ பூர்வம்: அனாதியில் மல மில்லாததையும் எல்லாமுடையதாயும் உள்ள சிவத்திற்கு என்னுடைய கரண உள்ளங்களைச் சமர்ப்பிக்கிறேன் என்பது. உத்தரம் உத்தரோத்தர மென்னும் பொருளுக்கு விவரம் இனிச் சுத்த சன்மார்க்கத்தில் வெளிப்படும்.
translation: In religion, the meaning of the phrase Sivayanama is of 4 kinds: purvam, purva-purvam, uttaram and uttarottaram. Purvam: "I bow to Siva." Purva-purvam: "I offer my inner faculties to Sivam, which from beginningless time is without impurity and has all." The detail of the meanings called uttaram and uttarottaram will come out hereafter in Suddha Sanmarkkam.
commentary: Religion keeps only the first two of the four meanings, bowing to Siva and offering the faculties to Him. The two later meanings, this shorter record says, will come out hereafter in Suddha Sanmarkkam.

blocks.html: The Five Letters and the Attainments (பஞ்சாக்ஷரமும் சித்தியும்)

tamil: சிவாயநம வென்னும் மந்திரத்துக்குப் பொருள் முன்போல் 4 வகை. அதில் பூர்வமாவது: சி என்பது பதி, வா சத்தி, ய ஜீவன், ந திரோதை, ம மாயை. பூர்வ பூர்வமாவது: சி யென்பது எல்லாமுடையது, வ என்பது அபின்னமாகிய அருள், ய ஆன்மாவாகிய சபை, ந ஜீவன், ம பசு, உத்தரத்தின் பொருள்: பரவிந்து பரநாதம் பரத்திலும், அபரவிந்து அபரநாதம் பூர்வத்திலும் வழங்கும். இவ்வளவும் சிவத் தியானமல்ல. தத்துவ அனுசந்தானமே. உத்தரத்தில் ஏமசித்தியும் உத்தரோத்தரத்தில் தேகசித்தியும் சொல்லுவது மத சன்மார்க்க அனுஷ்டானமாம். பஞ்சாக்ஷரத்தில் ஏமசித்தியும் தேகசித்தியும் சொல்வதற்குப் பிரமாணம்: "சிவாயநம வெனச் செம்பு பொன்னாயிடும்" "சிவாயநம வெனச் சிந்தித்திருப்பார்க்கு அபாயம் ஒருநாளுமில்லை". ஆதலால் பரிபாஷையால் மறுத்தது. மேற்குறித்த ஏமசித்தியும் தேகசித்தியும் எக்காலத்தும் இருக்கும்படியாகச் சொல்வது சுத்த சன்மார்க்கப் பூர்வோத்தரம்.
translation: The meaning of the mantra Sivayanama is of 4 kinds, as before. Of these, the purvam is: si is the Lord, va is Sakti, ya is the jeeva, na is the veiling power, ma is maya. The purva-purvam is: si is that which has all, va is grace, which is inseparable, ya is the Hall that is the soul, na is the jeeva, ma is the pasu. The meaning of the uttaram: the para-bindu and para-nada are at work in the para, and the apara-bindu and apara-nada in the purva.

All this is not meditation on Siva. It is only contemplation of the tattvas. To speak of hema siddhi in the uttaram and deha siddhi in the uttarottaram is the practice of the Sanmarkkam of the creeds. The authority for saying that the five letters speak of hema siddhi and deha siddhi: "Say Sivayanama, and copper turns to gold." "For those who keep thinking Sivayanama, there is no danger on any day." Therefore it was veiled in code language. To speak of this hema siddhi and deha siddhi as remaining for all time is the first and the later meaning of Suddha Sanmarkkam.
commentary: This record repeats the scheme and adds his sharpest sentence on it. "All this is not meditation on Siva. It is only contemplation of the tattvas." Every meaning the creeds draw from the letters, the map of release included, still works inside the tattvas, the constituents of body and world (note 56 reads the word itself). Meditation on Siva is another thing.

Anusandhanam, contemplation, is close and steady inner attention to something. The tattvas deserve that attention, and note 55 says experience dawns when they are crossed. Here the coded speech is called a veil, and lasting gold and a lasting body are once more given to Suddha Sanmarkkam.

tamil: ஓம் சிவாயநம என்று சதா சிந்தித்துக் கொண்டிருத்தல் வேண்டும். இவ்வுலகம் அருட்சத்தி, பொருட்சத்தி, கிரியாசத்தி, யோக சத்தி, ஞானசத்தி மயமாக இருப்பதாகப் பார்த்துக் கொண்டிருத்தல் வேண்டும். யோகம் செய்தல் வேண்டுவதில்லை. அதில் அழுந்தி விட்டால் மீளுவது கஷ்டம். சதா சிவக்கலப்பாய்க் கிடந்தாலும் மீளுதல் அருமை. மூடம் உண்டாகும். உண்மை.
translation: One must keep thinking "Om Sivayanama" at all times. One must keep seeing this world as made of the power of grace, the power of substance, the power of action, the power of yoga and the power of wisdom. There is no need to practice yoga. If one sinks into it, it is hard to come back. Even if one lies merged in Siva always, coming back is rare. Dullness arises. This is the truth.
commentary: Practical counsel, and some of the plainest in the book. Keep "Om Sivayanama" in mind at all times. Look at the world as made of five powers, arul sakti, the power of grace, porul sakti, the power of substance, and the powers of action, yoga and wisdom. Grace comes first in his list.

Then a warning that may surprise readers who think of spiritual life as yoga. There is no need to practice yoga, he says. One who sinks into it finds it hard to come back. Even one who lies always merged in Siva rarely returns, and mudam sets in, a dull stupor. He ends with one word, "Truth".
In plain terms, keep the mantra running quietly through the day, see the world around you as the working of God's powers, and do not chase states of trance that leave the mind dull.

tamil: ஓம் என்னும் எழுத்து பிரணவம் என்று சொல்லப்படும். படைத்தளித்தழிக்க வல்ல தலைவன் என்பதே அந்த ஓங்காரத்தின் பொருள்.
translation: The letter Om is called the Pranava. The meaning of that Omkara is this: the Lord who is able to create, to sustain and to destroy.
commentary: Om is the Pranava, the primal syllable spoken at the start of Vedic and Saiva rites, and Omkaram is its name as a letter. Vallalar gives its meaning in one line. Om names the Lord who is able to create, to sustain and to destroy. Note 49 opened the letter si in a similar way, and the next record opens Om.

tamil: பிரணவத்தின் ஐந்து பாகம் யாவெனில்:- அகரம், உகரம், மகரம், விந்து, நாதம். பஞ்சமி என்னும் வாக்கு பிரணவத்தின்கண் இருந்து தோன்றியது. அதற்கு ஸ்தானம் மூலாதாரம். அதிலிருந்து தோன்றிய மற்ற நான்கும் சூக்குமை, பைசந்தி, மத்திமை, வைகரி. இவற்றிற்கு இடம் நாபி, இருதயம், கண்டம், லலாடம்.
translation: The five parts of the Pranava are a, u, m, bindu and nada. The speech called panchami arose from the Pranava. Its seat is the muladhara. The other four that arose from it are sukshmai, paisanti, madhyamai and vaikari. Their places are the navel, the heart, the throat and the forehead.
commentary: Om has five parts. Three are its sounds a, u and m, which blend into o when spoken. The last two are bindu and nada, the seed-point and the primal sound (see note 1).

Indian teaching on sound usually names four levels of speech, from the deepest and most silent to the spoken word. Vallalar names five. Panchami, the fifth, comes straight from the Pranava and has its seat at the muladhara, the root centre at the base of the body. From it arise sukshmai, the subtle, then paisanti and madhyamai, and last vaikari, the spoken word. Their seats are the navel, the heart, the throat and the forehead, in that order.
Read upward, it is a picture of a word being born. It starts as Om at the root of the body and rises stage by stage until it is spoken. In his list the spoken word has its place at the forehead.
The speech that arose from the Pranava
The five parts of the Pranava are a, u, m, bindu and nada.
1. Panchami, which arose from the Pranava: its seat is the muladhara.
2. Sukshmai: at the navel.
3. Paisanti: at the heart.
4. Madhyamai: at the throat.
5. Vaikari: at the forehead.

tamil: மூலாங்கப் பிரணவமாகிய அகர லக்ஷணம் ஒருவாறு:-
ஊன்றல் வாமை.
சுழித்தல் ஜேஷ்டை.
விசிரிம்பித்தல் ரௌத்திரி.
மடித்து மேலேறல் காளி.
அங்கிருந்து கீழ்வரல் கலவிகரணி.
மேல் புடைபெயர்த்தல் பலவிகரணி.
கீழ்த்தாழல் பலப்பிரமதனி.
கீழ் ஊன்றி நிற்றல் சர்வபூததமனி.
வரிவடிவாதல் மனோன்மனி.
translation: The marks of the letter a, the Pranava of the root limb, in outline:-
Planting is Vamai.
Whirling is Jyeshtai.
Spreading open is Raudri.
Folding and rising up is Kali.
Coming down from there is Kalavikarani.
Pushing out above is Balavikarani.
Sinking below is Balapramathani.
Standing planted below is Sarvabhutadamani.
Taking the written form is Manonmani.
commentary: The letter a opens the alphabets of India, and the first verse of the Thirukkural says that all letters have a as their first. Vallalar calls it the root Pranava. He describes its coming into being as nine movements and gives each the name of a Sakti, a power of God.

The nine names are a fixed set in Saiva temple worship, the nine powers invoked on the seat of Siva, from Vamai to Manonmani. Here they become stages in the making of a letter. It is planted, it whirls, it spreads open, folds and rises, comes down, pushes out above, sinks below, stands firm at the bottom and at last takes written form.
Readers who write Tamil may see in these movements the strokes of the letter itself, though Vallalar does not say so. He gives the list as an outline and adds no comment of his own.

tamil: இதில் விந்து நாதம் முதலிய நவநிலைகளுமுள.
அகரம்
அகரமாகிய முதல் எழுத்து உற்பத்தி விவரம்:-
விந்து - பெரிய வெளிச்சம், சூரிய வெளிச்சம்.
நாதம் - பெரியநாதம்.
பரவிந்து - அதில் பாதி வெளிச்சம், சந்திர வெளிச்சம். பரநாதம் - நாதம்.
அபரவிந்து - வெளிச்சம், நக்ஷத்திர ஒளி.
அபரநாதம் - நாதம்.
திக்கிராந்தம் - அருகியவெளிச்சம், மின்னல் ஒளி.
அதிக்கிராந்தம் - சப்தம்.
translation: In this there are also the nine states, bindu, nada and the rest.
The letter a
How the first letter, a, comes into being:-
Bindu: the great light, the light of the sun.
Nada: the great sound.
Para-bindu: half of that light, the light of the moon. Para-nada: sound.
Apara-bindu: light, the light of the stars.
Apara-nada: sound.
Dikkirantam: a scant light, the light of lightning.
Atikkirantam: sound.
commentary: Light and sound come here in pairs, and the pairs are the "nine states, bindu, nada and the rest" that he has just announced. The highest bindu is the great light, the light of the sun, with the great nada beside it. Para-bindu is half that light, the moon's. Apara-bindu is starlight. Dikkirantam is a thin, scant light, the flash of lightning, and atikkirantam is its sound.

Note 1 matched the four lights of the sky with the layers of a person and placed bindu and nada in lightning and thunder. Here the same lights mark grades in the birth of a single letter. Only four pairs, eight states, are given for the nine he names.

tamil: 9. வாமசத்தி
10. ஜேஷ்ட சத்தி.
11. ரௌத்திரி சத்தி.
translation: 9. Vama Sakti.
10. Jyeshta Sakti.
11. Raudri Sakti.
12. Kali Sakti.
commentary: The numbering runs from 9 to 12 and names four of the nine powers listed above, Vama, Jyeshta, Raudri and Kali. It seems the four pairs of light and sound were counted as 1 to 8. The list stops at Kali, and the printed note gives no more.

tamil: காயத்ரி: கா-ய-த்ரி. க ஜலதத்துவமாகிய ஸ்தூலதேகம், பிரமஸ்வரூபம். ய வாயுதத்துவமாகிய சூக்ஷ்மதேகம், விஷ்ணு ஸ்வரூபம். ஆ அக்னிதத்துவமாகிய காரணதேகம், ருத்ரஸ்வரூபம். த்ரி மூன்று. அதாவது, மேற்குறித்த மூன்று தேகங்களின் ஸ்வரூப ரூபசுபாவ குணங்களை ஐயம் திரிபு மயக்க மின்றிக் கடந்தால், ஜனனமரண சாகரம் நீங்கி நித்தியர் ஆவோம். எப்படியெனில்: காயத்திரி மந்திரத்திற்குப் பாதம் மூன்று. பாதம் ஒன்றிற்கு வர்ணம் எட்டு. ஆக மூன்று பாதத்திற்கும் வர்ணம் இருபத்து நான்கு. பாதம் மூன்றென்பதன் குறிப்பு: ஜீவர்களுக்கு மலம் மூன்று. வருணம் இருபத்து நான்கு என்பதன் குறிப்பு: ஜீவர்களுக்கு மலம் மூன்று. வருணம் இருபத்து நான்கு என்பதன் குறிப்பு: இரு - இரண்டு, ஜீவகாருண்யம் தத்துவவிசாரம் ஆகிய இரண்டையும்; பத்து (பற்று) - பிடி, பற்றினால்; நான்கு - நாலாகிய ஜீவகாருண்யம், ஈசுரபக்தி, பாச வைராக்கியம், பிரம ஞானம் ஆகிய இவற்றை அடையலாம். அடைந்து, காயத்ரிமந்திரம் திரிமூர்த்தி ஸ்வரூபமாதலால், இதற்கு அதீதமான பிரமானுபவத்தைப் பெறலாம்.
translation: Gayatri: kaa-ya-tri. Ka is the gross body, which is of the water tattva, the form of Brahma. Ya is the subtle body, which is of the air tattva, the form of Vishnu. Aa is the causal body, which is of the fire tattva, the form of Rudra. Tri is three. That is, if we pass beyond the essence, form, nature and qualities of these three bodies without doubt, error or confusion, we leave the ocean of birth and death and become eternal.

How? The Gayatri mantra has three feet. Each foot has eight letters, so the three feet have twenty-four letters. The sign in the three feet: souls have three impurities. The sign in the twenty-four letters: iru, two, that is, both Jeevakarunyam and inquiry into the tattvas; pattu (patru), grip, by gripping these; nangu, four, one can reach the four, Jeevakarunyam, devotion to God, detachment from the bond and knowledge of Brahman. Having reached them, since the Gayatri mantra is the form of the three gods, one can gain the experience of Brahman that is beyond it.
commentary: The Gayatri is the most honored mantra of the Vedas, twenty-four syllables in three lines of eight. Vallalar reads it in his own key, starting from the Tamil spelling of its name. Ka is the gross body, made of the water tattva, and its form is Brahma. Ya is the subtle body, made of air, the form of Vishnu. Aa is the causal body, made of fire, the form of Rudra. Tri is three.

Gross, subtle and causal are the three bodies Indian teaching gives to every person, from the physical frame to the deepest seed of the self. Cross all three, their essence, form, nature and qualities, with no doubt or confusion left, and the ocean of birth and death is left behind.

Then he plays on numbers. The three lines stand for the three impurities of souls (see note 49). The Tamil for twenty-four, irupattu nangu, he hears as three words. Iru is two, pattu heard as patru is a grip, and nangu is four. Grip two things, Jeevakarunyam and inquiry into the tattvas, and you reach four, Jeevakarunyam, devotion to God, detachment from the bonds and the knowledge of Brahman.

Jeevakarunyam heads both lists. It is what one holds to and also what one arrives at. Because the mantra is the form of the three gods, the experience it points to lies beyond them, in Brahman. The practice is inside the note. Hold to compassion for living beings and keep up the inquiry.

tamil: மேலும், தத்துவ த்ரேயங்களான மூன்று தேகங்களுக்கும் தத்துவம் யா தெனில்:- வர்ணம் இருபத்துநான்கு. ஆதலால், ஸ்தூலதத்துவம் இருபத்துநான்கு. பாதம் மூன்று, காயத்ரி திரி மூர்த்தி ஸ்வரூபம், இவற்றுள் ஒன்றில் ஒன்றைக் கொடுக்கவந்தது ஒன்று:- 3,3,1 ஆகிய இவற்றைச் சேர்க்க ஏழு ஆகிறது. ஆதலால், சூட்சும தத்துவம் ஏழு. இதற்குச் சத்தி மூன்று. அநுபவசத்தி ஒன்று, சமத்துவம் ஒன்று. ஆக ஐந்து. ஆதலால் காரணதேக தத்துவம் ஐந்து. மேற்குறித்த முப்பத்தாறு தத்துவங்களையுங் கடந்தால், அனுபவம் விளங்கும். எப்படியெனில்:- ஓதயாத்: ஓ ஆன்மஅறிவின்கண், த சத்துவ குணமயமாய், த் அருளனுபவம் பெற்று, யா பிரமமாதல். ஆதலால், மேற்குறித்த காயத்திரியின் ஸ்வரூபானுபவத்தைப் பெறுதலாம்.
translation: Further, what are the tattvas of the three bodies, which are the triad of tattvas? The letters are twenty-four, so the gross tattvas are twenty-four. The feet are three, and the Gayatri is the form of the three gods; and among these, that which came to give one within the other is one. Adding 3, 3 and 1 makes seven, so the subtle tattvas are seven. For this there are three powers, one power of experience and one of sameness: five in all. So the tattvas of the causal body are five. If we pass beyond these thirty-six tattvas, experience will dawn.

How? Odayat: o, in the soul's knowledge; da, becoming full of sattva; t, gaining the experience of grace; yaa, becoming Brahman. So one can gain the experience of the true nature of the Gayatri named above.
commentary: Twenty-four, seven and five make thirty-six. This is the classic count of the tattvas in Saiva Siddhanta, twenty-four atma tattvas of body and mind, seven vidya tattvas and five Siva tattvas at the top. Vallalar draws all three numbers out of the Gayatri. Twenty-four letters give the gross tattvas. Three lines, three gods and one more give the seven subtle ones. Three powers with a power of experience and a power of sameness give the five of the causal body.

Cross all thirty-six and experience dawns. He then reads the word odayat, which looks like the end of the mantra's last word, prachodayat. O is the soul's knowledge, da the state full of sattva, the clear quality, t the experience of grace, and yaa becoming Brahman. Four sounds trace the climb, and the reading, again, is his own.

tamil: தத்துவமென்பது: தத்*தவம் = தத்துவம். தத் - அது. அது வென்பது சிவம். த்வம் - அதன்தன்மை. ஆதலால், தத்துவம் என்பது சிவத்தின் தன்மை.
translation: Tattvam means this: tat + tvam = tattvam. Tat is "that", and "that" is Sivam. Tvam is its nature. So tattvam means the nature of Sivam.
commentary: Tattva is one of the most used words in this book. It names the principles, the working parts, from which bodies and worlds are made, and note 19 reads every Purana as their conquest. Here Vallalar asks what the word itself means.

He splits it as tat and tvam. Tat is "that", and "that" is Sivam. Tvam is its nature. So a tattva is the nature of Sivam. Sanskrit grammar builds the word from tat and the suffix -tva, "-ness", giving "thatness", the real nature of a thing. His reading stays close to that and names what "that" is.
The consequence is worth weighing. The tattvas that note 55 asks us to cross are still, by their very name, the nature of Sivam.

tamil: குடிலை என்பது மூலப் பிரகிருதி.
translation: Kudilai is primal nature.
commentary: Kudilai is a word from Saiva and siddha writing for the subtle source out of which the worlds unfold. Vallalar fixes it in one line as mula prakriti, primal nature, the root from which the elements and the rest of creation come forth. Note 58 turns to the elements.

tamil: பூதம் என்பது: பூ-த-ம். பூ அலர்ந்தது, த தடித்தது, ம் கலத்தல், ஆதலால், எங்கும் நிறைந்து அணுவாய்க் கலத்தல் பூதம்.
translation: Bhutam means this: bhu-ta-m. Bhu, opened out; ta, thickened; m, mingling. So bhutam is that which fills everywhere and mingles as atoms.
commentary: Bhutam is an element, one of the five, earth, water, fire, air and space. In Sanskrit the word comes from a root meaning "to become". Vallalar reads it through its Tamil sounds. Bhu also means a flower, so it is what has blossomed or opened out. Ta is what has thickened, and m is mingling. An element is what opens, thickens and mingles until it fills every place, down to the atom. Note 36 has already given the atom to Brahma.

blocks.html: The Meaning of the Word Bhuta (பூதம் என்பதன் சப்தார்த்தம்)

tamil: பூதமென்பது யாது? அதனது சொரூப ரூப சுபாவங்களென்ன? பூதம் என்பதற்குச் சப்தார்த்தம்: பூ மலர்ந்தது, பிரகாசம்; த தடித்தது, காரியம்; ம் ஊன்றியது, நிலை. இதற்குத் தாத்பரியம்: நிலை பெற்ற காரியம் பிரகாசம். பூத அக்கினித் தோற்றமென்றும் பெயர். பூதகாரிய அக்கினி என்றும் பெயர். பூ என்பதில் உகர உயிரும் தம் என்பதில் அகர உயிரும் எண்ணில் அ - ம், உ - ம் ஆயின, ஆக தொகை 10. இந்தப் பத்து இடத்திலும் பூதகாரிய அக்கினித் தோற்றம் உண்டு. கல்லுக்குள்ளிருக்கிற நெருப்பு பஞ்சில் காரியப்படுவது போலாம். பத்துப் பொது ஸ்தானங்களாவன: மண், ஜலம், அக்கினி, காற்று, வெளி, பிரகிருதி, மாயை, சூரியன், சந்திரன், நக்ஷத்திரம் ஆக இடம் 10.
translation: What is a bhutam? What are its essence, form and nature? The word-meaning of bhutam: bhu, blossomed, that is, light; ta, thickened, that is, effect; m, planted, that is, steadiness. Its sense: light that has become a steady effect. It is also named the appearance of elemental fire. It is also named the fire that is the effect of the elements.

If the vowel u in bhu and the vowel a in tam are counted as numbers, they become a and u, and the total is 10. In all these ten places the fire that is the effect of the elements appears, as the fire inside a stone comes into action in cotton. The ten common places are earth, water, fire, air, space, prakriti, maya, the sun, the moon and the stars: ten places.
commentary: A fuller record of the same word, and now each sound carries a second meaning. Bhu is blossoming and so light. Ta is thickening and so effect. M is being planted and so steadiness. An element is light that has become a steady effect. That is why he also calls it the appearance of elemental fire, a fire hidden inside every element.

The number ten comes from Tamil numerals, where the letter a stands for 8 and u for 2. The two vowels hidden in the word, u in bhu and a in tam, add up to ten. So he names ten places where the hidden fire works, the five elements, prakriti, maya, the sun, the moon and the stars.
His image is the fire in a stone. It sits inside, unseen, until the stone strikes and the cotton catches. In the same way the fire of the elements waits in all ten places for its moment to act.
The ten places where elemental fire appears
1. Earth. 2. Water. 3. Fire. 4. Air. 5. Space. 6. Prakriti. 7. Maya. 8. The sun. 9. The moon. 10. The stars.
11. In these ten places the fire that is the effect of the elements appears, as the fire inside a stone comes into action in cotton.
Bhutam means light that has become a steady effect.

tamil: பௌதிக மென்பது லிங்கமாதி உபரசம் நூற்றிருபதிற்கும், பாஷாணமாதி 64 பாஷாணங்கட்கும், சுக்காதி ஓஷதி மூல பத்திர பீசங்கட்கும் பெயர். இஃது ஒருவாறு பூதகாரிய தேகமாதி தத்துவங்கட்கும் பெயர். பெளாதீ் அகம் = பௌதீகம். பெள - மூடல், அகம் - உள், தீ - அக்கினி, ஆதலால் தீயை உள்ளடக்கியது பௌதீகம். தீ என்பது காரண உஷ்ணம்.
பௌதிகங்கள் பௌதிகங்க ளென்பவை வீரம் பூரம் முதலிய 64 சரக்குகள்.
translation: Bhautikam is the name for the hundred and twenty secondary minerals beginning with cinnabar, for the 64 mineral poisons, pashanam and the rest, and for the herbs, roots, leaves and seeds beginning with dry ginger. In a sense it is also the name for the tattvas, the body and the rest, which are effects of the elements.
Bau + thi + akam = bhautikam. Bau means covering, akam inside, thi fire. So bhautikam is that which holds fire inside. Fire here means causal heat.
Bhautikams: the bhautikams are the 64 drugs such as viram and puram.
commentary: Bhautikam comes from bhuta, an element, and means "elemental", anything made of the elements. In the hands of a Siddha physician the word covers the whole pharmacy. Siddha medicine, the old Tamil system of healing, sorts its materials into secondary minerals, pashanams or mineral poisons, and the herbs with their roots, leaves and seeds. Vallalar names all of these, and then adds the body, since it too is made of the elements.

His reading of the syllables is his own. The usual derivation is simply from bhuta. He hears thi, fire, inside the word, and bau, a covering, wrapped round it. A medicine is a substance that holds fire, and so is the human body. That fire he calls causal heat, kaarana ushnam. In note 7's table fire was already the cause among the three lights, and note 1 placed fire at the innermost place of the cosmos.
The last line is a shorter record of the same teaching. It counts 64 drugs, where the main passage counted 64 mineral poisons. Viram and puram are two mercury preparations of Siddha medicine.

tamil: நினைப்பு மறைப்பு உண்டாவதற்குக் காரணம்: சந்திரன் அக்கினியோடு கூடி, சூரியபாகத்திலுண்டாகும் காற்றினால் அசைக்கப்படும் போது, உண்டாகும் நினைப்பு; சூரியன் அக்கினியோடு கூடி, சந்திர பாகத்தில் உண்டாகுங் காற்றினால் அசைக்கப்படும்போது உண்டாகின்றது மறைப்பு. நினைப்பு மறைப்பு என்பதற்குப் பொருள்: நினைப்பென்பது யாது? ஜனனம், மன அசைவு, ஒன்றை நினைத்தல், சகலகாலம், மேற்படி தத்துவம் வேறொன்றில் பற்றல், தத்துவத்தின் அசைவாகிய ஆவி மேலேறுதல், மேற்படி ஆவி ஏறின இடத்தில் நில்லாது அக்கிரமித்தல். மறைப்பென்பது யாது? மரணம், தூக்கம், மனம் ஒன்றைப்பற்றி உடனே மறைதல், கேவலகாலம், மேற்படி தத்துவத்தின் கூர்மை கீழ்ச்செல்லுதல், பிரக்ஞை இல்லாதிருத்தல், மேற்படி ஆவி அக்கிரமித்தல், மனம் ஆபாசப்பட்டுச் சூனியமாதல். மேற்குறித்த நினைப்பு மறைப் பற்று நிரதிசயானந்தமாய் அருள்வடிவாவதே சுத்த சன்மார்க்க சாதனம்.

நினைப்பு மறைப்பு இந்த ஜீவன் அக்கினியின் சூரியபாகத்தி லுண்டாகும் காற்றினால் அசைக்கப்படும்போது நினைப்பும், அக்கினியின் சந்திரபாகத்தில் உண்டாகுங் காற்றினால் அசைக்கப்படும் போது மறைப்பும் உண்டாகின்றன. இதுதான் நினைப்பு மறைப்பு உண்டாவதற்குக் காரணம்.
translation: The cause of the arising of thinking and forgetting: when the moon joins fire and is stirred by the air that arises in the sun's part, thinking arises. When the sun joins fire and is stirred by the air that arises in the moon's part, forgetting arises.

The meaning of thinking and forgetting. What is thinking? Birth, the stirring of the mind, thinking of one thing, the sakala state, the tattva named above clinging to something else, the vapor, which is the stirring of the tattva, rising upward, and that vapor not staying where it rose but overrunning it.

What is forgetting? Death, sleep, the mind taking hold of a thing and at once losing it, the kevala state, the sharpness of the tattva going downward, being without awareness, the vapor overrunning, the mind growing foul and becoming empty. To be rid of this thinking and forgetting, and to become the form of grace as bliss that nothing surpasses, is the practice of Suddha Sanmarkkam.

Thinking and forgetting: when this jeeva is stirred by the air that arises in the sun's part of the fire, thinking arises. When it is stirred by the air that arises in the moon's part of the fire, forgetting arises. This is the cause of the arising of thinking and forgetting.
commentary: Ninaippu is thinking, the mind turned toward something. Maraippu is forgetting, the mind turned away and going dark. Note 11 said that every birth turns on these two. This note shows how far the pair reaches.

Look at the two lists side by side. Birth, waking thought, the sakala state and the vapor rising stand on one side. Death, sleep, the kevala state and the mind sinking stand on the other. Sakala is the soul joined to body and faculties, kevala the soul alone in its darkness (see note 7). The same swing runs at every scale. A thought seized and dropped a moment later is a small birth and a small death, and a lifetime is the same movement drawn out long.

The cause is given in body terms. Sun, moon and fire, the three lights of notes 1 and 7, work inside us, and an air rising in the sun's part or the moon's part stirs them. These parts are most likely the solar and lunar sides of the body that note 7 described.

Vallalar does not ask the seeker to choose the bright side of the swing. He asks to be rid of both, and to become the form of grace in a bliss nothing surpasses. That, he says, is the practice of Suddha Sanmarkkam.
The closing lines are a shorter record. They put the jeeva in place of the moon and sun, and the account stays the same.

tamil: நினைப்பு மறைப்பு என்பதற்குப் பொருள்: நினைப்பென்பது ஜனனம், மனம் நினைத்தல், சகலம், தத்துவத்தின் ஆவி அதிக்கிரமிக்கிறது. மறைப்பென்பதற்குப் பொருள்: மரணம், கேவலம், தூக்கம், தத்துவத்தின் கூறுபாடு கீழ்ச்செல்லுதல், பிரக்ஞை யில்லாதிருத்தல், அதனது உஷ்ணம் அதிக்கிரமிக்கிறது, மனம் ஆபாசப்பட்டுக் கீழ்ச்செல்லுதல். ஆதலால், நினைப்பு மறைப்பு அற்று, நிரதிசயானந்தமாய் அருள்வடிவமாவதே சுத்தசன்மார்க்க சாதனம் இது ஒருவாறு.
translation: The meaning of thinking and forgetting: thinking is birth, the mind thinking, the sakala state, the vapor of the tattva overrunning. The meaning of forgetting: death, the kevala state, sleep, the parts of the tattva going downward, being without awareness, its heat overrunning, the mind growing foul and going downward. So, to be rid of thinking and forgetting and to become the form of grace as bliss that nothing surpasses is the practice of Suddha Sanmarkkam. This is one way of putting it.
commentary: Lists and verdict survive here almost word for word, with small changes. Forgetting now ends in heat overrunning, where the main passage had the vapor, and the tattva's "sharpness" has become its "parts", a slip of the ear perhaps. The last words, "this is one way of putting it", sound like the listener admitting that his short note leaves things out.
How thinking and forgetting arise
1. Thinking: when the moon joins fire and is stirred by the air that arises in the sun's part, thinking arises; the vapor of the tattva rises upward. It is birth, the sakala state.
2. Forgetting: when the sun joins fire and is stirred by the air that arises in the moon's part, forgetting arises; the tattva goes downward. It is death, sleep, the kevala state.
To be rid of both and become the form of grace as bliss is the practice of Suddha Sanmarkkam.

tamil: விருப்பு வெறுப்பு என்பதற்குப் பொருள்: விருப்பென்பது யாது? ஒன்றை வேண்டிப் பந்தப்பட்டு, பூரண லக்பியத்தை விட்டு, அதிசயமாகப் பார்த்து நிற்றல். இந்த விருப்பால் தானுங் கெட்டு, இதர வஸ்துவுங் கெட்டு, சாதனமுந் தடைப்பட்டுவிடும். எவ்வகையிலும் விருப்பென்பது கூடாது. வெறுப்பென்பது யாது? வேண்டாமை, துவேஷம், இதர வஸ்துவைப் பற்றாதிருத்தல். இந்த வெறுப்பால் இதரவஸ்துவிடத்தில் துவேஷந் தோன்றி ஜீவோபகாரத்தைத் தடை செய்யும். ஆகையால் வெறுப்புங் கூடாது. மேற்குறித்த இரண்டு மற்று, சத்துவமயமாய் நிற்றல்வேண்டும்.
translation: The meaning of liking and disliking. What is liking? Wanting a thing, becoming bound, leaving the full goal, and standing to gaze at it in wonder. By this liking one ruins oneself, the other thing is ruined too, and the practice is blocked. Liking must not be, in any way.

What is disliking? Not wanting, hatred, not taking hold of another thing. By this disliking, hatred arises toward the other thing and blocks help to living beings. So disliking must not be either. One must be free of both and stand filled with sattva.
commentary: Viruppu is liking, veruppu disliking. Vallalar takes each apart and counts the damage.

Liking begins with wanting, and wanting binds. The bound mind forgets its full goal and stands staring at one thing in wonder, the way a child stops dead at a sweet stall. Three things suffer. The person is ruined, the thing liked is spoiled by being grabbed, and the practice stops.

Disliking does its harm another way. It turns into hatred, and hatred, he says, blocks jeevopakaram, help given to living beings. A person who has taken against someone will not feed them. So disliking is forbidden for the sake of compassion, as liking is forbidden for the sake of the goal.

Sattva is the clear quality, the first of the three gunas (see note 55). Note 68, a little further on, defines it as standing as oneself. When a pull or a push rises in the mind, the practice is to come back to that, standing as oneself, neither reaching nor recoiling.

tamil: விருப்பு வெறுப்பு என்பதற்குப் பொருள்: விருப்பென்பது வேண்டுதல், பந்தம். பூர்ணபாவனையை விட்டு அதிசயமாகப் பார்த்து விரும்புதலால் பூர்ணபாவனை தடைப்பட்டுத் தான் கெடுவன். ஆதலால் விருப்பென்பது எவ்வளவும் கூடாது. வெறுப்பென்பது வேண்டாமை, துவேஷம், எதிர்கண்ட வஸ்துவைப் பற்றாதிருத்தல். இதரவஸ்துவைக் கெடுதலென்று நினைப்பதால் வெறுப்பென்பதும் கூடாது. விருப்பு வெறுப்பு அற்று அருள்வடிவாவதே சுத்த சன்மார்க்கம்.
translation: The meaning of liking and disliking: liking is wanting, bondage. Leaving the contemplation of fullness and liking a thing, gazing at it in wonder, blocks the contemplation of fullness, and one ruins oneself. So liking must not be, to any degree. Disliking is not wanting, hatred, not taking hold of the thing one meets. Because one then thinks of the other thing as harm, disliking must not be either. To be free of liking and disliking and to become the form of grace is Suddha Sanmarkkam.
commentary: This shorter record names what liking interrupts. It is purna bhavanai, the contemplation of fullness, the very practice of note 1, which sees God's light filling body and cosmos alike. Disliking is faulted for making us see other things as harmful. The record ends with the form of grace, where the main passage ended with sattva.

tamil: சங்கல்பத்தின் பொருளும் விரிவும் யாதெனில்:- விரிவாவது ஐந்து: நிர்விகல்பம், சவிகல்பம், சங்கல்பம், விகல்பம், கல்பம். இவற்றுள் நிர்விகல்பமாவது கடவுளறிவு. மேற்படி அறிவின் வியாபகமே சவிகல்பம். சங்கல்ப மென்பது கரணம் யாதொன்றிலும் பற்றாமல் சுத்தமாயிருந்த காலத்தில் தோன்றிய அசைவே சங்கல்பம்; ஒன்றிலும் பற்றாது அசைந்த மேலசைவென்னும் புடைபெயர்ச்சியே சங்கல்பம். நாம் நஷ்டமடையோம் என்று உள்ளழுந்திய பிரக்ஞையே சங்கல்பம். விகல்ப மென்பது பிரம சதாசிவ கால அளவைக் குறித்தது. இதில் பலவாக விரிந்த அனுசந்தானங்கள் கல்பம். உள்ளழுந்தல், அதைச் சிந்தித்தல் சிந்தித்தலை விசாரித்தல் இம்மூன்றுமே சங்கல்ப விகல்ப கல்பம்.
translation: What is the meaning of sankalpa, and its spread? Its spread is five: nirvikalpa, savikalpa, sankalpa, vikalpa and kalpa. Of these, nirvikalpa is the knowledge of God. The pervading of that knowledge is savikalpa.

Sankalpa is the stir that arose at the time when the faculty was pure and clung to nothing. The upward stir, a shifting that moved while clinging to nothing, is sankalpa. The awareness sunk deep within, that we shall not perish, is sankalpa.

Vikalpa refers to the measure of time of Brahma and Sadasiva. The contemplations spread out within it in many ways are kalpa. Sinking within, thinking on it, and inquiring into that thinking, these three are sankalpa, vikalpa and kalpa.
commentary: In ordinary use sankalpa means a resolve or an intention. Before a temple rite the worshipper makes a sankalpa, stating what the rite is for. Vallalar takes the word much further down.

He starts from a family of five words built on the same root. Nirvikalpa, knowledge without division, is God's own knowing. Savikalpa, knowledge with distinctions, is that knowing spread out and pervading. Then comes sankalpa, which he defines three times over. It is the first stir of a faculty that is pure and holds on to nothing. It moves upward. And it carries one certainty, sunk deep inside, that we shall not perish. Karanam, the faculty, is the mind and its companions (see note 1).

Vikalpa usually means doubt or wavering, and kalpa a cosmic age, as in note 3. Vallalar gives both words his own sense here. Vikalpa is a measure of time on the scale of Brahma and Sadasiva, and kalpa the many contemplations within it.

The last sentence turns all this into three inner movements: sinking within, thinking on what is found there, and inquiring into that thinking. The next record of this note says which part of us does each.

tamil: மேற்குறித்த சங்கல்ப மயமா யிருந்தால் சிவானுபவம் பெறலாம். "சந்ததமும் வேதமொழி யாதொன்று பற்றி னதுதான் வந்துமுற்றும்"* என்றபடி.
தாயுமானவர் பாடல், கருணாக்கரக் கடவுள், 7.
translation: If one stays filled with this sankalpa, one can gain the experience of Siva, as it is said: "Always, says the word of the Veda, whatever one holds to, that very thing comes and is fulfilled."
Editor's note: Thayumanavar's songs, Karunakara Kadavul, verse 7.
commentary: What we hold to, we come to. Hold the certainty of not perishing and Sivanubhavam, the experience of Siva (see note 11), follows. Vallalar borrows the line from the Tamil saint-poet Thayumanavar, who gives it as the teaching of the Veda.

tamil: சங்கல்ப மென்பது 5 வகை. அதாவது நிர்விகல்பம் 1, சவிகல்பம் 2, சங்கல்பம் 3, விகல்பம் 4, கல்பம் 5. நிர்விகல்பமென்பது கடவுளறிவு. சவிகல்ப மென்பது அதினது வியாபகம். சங்கல்பமென்பது யாதொன்றிலும் பற்றாமல் சுத்தமாயிருந்த காலத்தில் தோன்றிய அசைவாகிய நினைப்பே, முன் அசைவின்றி அசைந்த அசைவாகிய மேலசை வென்னும் புடைபெயர்ச்சியே எக்காலத்தும் மரணமடைய மாட்டோமென்கிற பிரக்ஞையே. விகல்பம் என்பது பிரம சதாசிவ கால அளவைக் குறித்தது. கல்பம் என்பது மேற் குறித்தவைகளுக்கு அனுசந்தானங்கள். சங்கல்ப விகல்ப கல்பமென்பவை 3 வகை. உள் அழுந்தல் ஆன்ம திருஷ்டி, அதைச் சிந்தித்தல் ஜீவ திருஷ்டி, அதை விசாரித்தல் மனதிருஷ்டி. இந்த மூன்றுமே சங்கல்ப விகல்ப கல்பம். ஆதலால், மனத்தில் யாதொன்றும் இல்லாமல் சுத்த மனமாக, நாம் நஷ்டமடையமாட்டோ மென்று உள்ளமுந்தி நிச்சயித்தலே சங்கல்பம்.
translation: Sankalpa is of 5 kinds, that is, nirvikalpa 1, savikalpa 2, sankalpa 3, vikalpa 4, kalpa 5. Nirvikalpa is the knowledge of God. Savikalpa is its pervading. Sankalpa is the thought, a stir that arose at the time when one was pure and clung to nothing. It is the upward stir, the shifting, a stir that moved with no stir before it. It is the awareness that we shall never die at any time. Vikalpa refers to the measure of time of Brahma and Sadasiva. Kalpa is the contemplation of the things named above.

Sankalpa, vikalpa and kalpa are of 3 kinds. Sinking within is the sight of the soul. Thinking on it is the sight of the jeeva. Inquiring into it is the sight of the mind. These three are sankalpa, vikalpa and kalpa.
So, with nothing at all in the mind, the mind pure, to sink within and settle it for certain that we shall not perish, that is sankalpa.
commentary: What the main passage left out, this record supplies. The three inner movements belong to three parts of us. Sinking within is the soul's sight, thinking on it is the jeeva's, and inquiring into it is the mind's. Drishti, sight, follows the order of note 1, where the soul knows a thing's truth, the jeeva its use and the mind its name and qualities. The deepest of the three, the soul sinking inward, comes first.
One phrase is sharper here. The first stir is "a stir with no stir before it", the very first movement of a mind at rest.
Then the practice, in one sentence. Empty the mind of everything. Let it be pure. Sink inward, and there settle it for certain that we shall not perish.

tamil: பற்று மனத்தின் கூறுபாடு 4 வகை: அதாவது ஜீவப்பற்று, பந்துப் பற்று, களத்திரப்பற்று, தேகப்பற்று. தேகப்பற்றாகிய அகப்பற்றுப் போயிருத்தல் சங்கல்பம். சங்கல்பம் சங்கல்பமாவது: சம் - முடிவு; கல்பம் - காலபேதம்; கால முடிவு.
translation: Attachment, a part of the mind, is of 4 kinds, that is, attachment to life, attachment to kin, attachment to wife and attachment to the body. When attachment to the body, which is the inner attachment, has gone, that is sankalpa. How sankalpa is sankalpa: sam means end, kalpam the divisions of time, so sankalpa is the end of time.
commentary: Patru is attachment, the mind's grip on things. The four kinds move inward, from life in general, to kin, to wife, to one's own body. The body is the closest, and Vallalar calls it the inner attachment, using agam, the inner, from note 1. When even that grip has gone, sankalpa is reached.

His reading of the word is his own. Grammarians take it differently. For him sam is end and kalpam the divisions of time, so sankalpa is time's end. It fits the certainty this note keeps returning to, that we shall not perish. A mind that no longer clings to the body has stepped out of time's reckoning.

tamil: தன்னையும் தனக் காதாரமான தலைவனையும் கூடஸ்தனையும் தெரிந்து கொள்ளுதல் வேண்டும்.
translation: One must know oneself, the Lord who is one's support, and the kutastha.
commentary: Three things to know, in order: yourself, the Lord who holds you up, and the kutastha. The Sanskrit word means "standing like an anvil", the block that stays still while the metal is beaten on it. It names the changeless one in us, unmoved by all that happens around it. Note 64 sets the kutastha in its place among five grades of consciousness.

sections.title: The Union of Kutastha and Brahman

tamil: கேவல வேதாந்தத்தில் கூடஸ்த பிரம ஐக்கியத்தின் பொருள். ஜீவசைதன்யம், ஈசுரசைதன்யம், பிரமசைதன்யம், கூடஸ்தசைதன்யம், சர்வசாக்ஷி. இவற்றிற்குப் பிரதிநாமம் மேகாகாசம், ஜலாகாசம், கடாகாசம், தத்துவாகாசம், மஹாகாசம் ஆக ஐந்து. தம்பலப்பூச்சி முதல் மனுஷர்களில் மூடர் பரியந்தம் பரதந்திரர்கள், ஜீவசைதன்யம். சுராசுரர் அறிவுடைய ஜீவர்கள் சுதந்திரர்கள், இவர்கள் ஈசுரசைதன்யம். காரியம் ரூபம் முதலியவற்றோடு கூடிய சுத்ததேகி பிரமசைதன்யம். காரணகாரியம் ரூபாரூபம் முதலியவற்றுடனின்ற பிரணவதேகி கூடஸ்தசைதன்யம். காரணம் அரூபம் முதலியவாக நின்ற ஞானதேகி சர்வசாக்ஷி யெனக் கொள்க.
translation: The meaning of the union of kutastha and Brahman in kevala Vedanta. Jeeva consciousness, Ishvara consciousness, Brahma consciousness, kutastha consciousness, and the witness of all. Their other names are cloud-space, water-space, pot-space, tattva-space and great space, five in all.

From the tiny velvet mite up to the dull among human beings, those who depend on others are jeeva consciousness. Gods and asuras and souls with knowledge are independent, and they are Ishvara consciousness. The pure-bodied one, joined with effect, form and the rest, is Brahma consciousness. The Pranava-bodied one, standing with cause-and-effect, form-and-formless and the rest, is kutastha consciousness. Take the wisdom-bodied one, standing as cause, the formless and the rest, as the witness of all.
commentary: Kevala here means "alone, mere", a different use from the kevala state of note 7. Kevala Vedanta is Vedanta taken by itself, the school of non-duality. It speaks of the union of the kutastha, the changeless one in us (see note 63), with Brahman, the Absolute.

Chaitanya is consciousness. Vedanta teachers like to compare consciousness to space. Space inside a pot looks separate from the open sky, yet it is the same space. Vallalar lists five such grades with five names of space, from cloud-space up to great space.

Then he fills the grades with beings. At the bottom are those who depend on others, from the thambalappuchi, the little red velvet mite that appears after rain, up to the dullest of human beings. Above them are the independent, gods and asuras and souls with knowledge.

The top three are where his own teaching enters. He gives them the three bodies of grace that note 8 named, the pure body, the Pranava body and the wisdom body. The pure-bodied one still has form and belongs to effect. The Pranava-bodied one holds both. Cause and formless is the wisdom-bodied one, and Vallalar calls that one the witness of all. A Vedanta scheme becomes a ladder of attainment that a human being can climb.

tamil: ஜீவ சைதன்னியம் - மேகாகாசம்
ஈசுர சைதன்னியம் - ஜலாகாசம்
பிரம சைதன்னியம் - கடாகாசம்
கூடஸ்த சைதன்னியம் - தத்துவாகாசம்
சர்வசாக்ஷி - மகாகாசம்

ஜீவ சைதன்னியம் - தம்பப்பூச்சி முதல் மனிதரில் மூடர் பரியந்தம், பரதந்திரர்கள் ஈசுர சைதன்னியம் - அசுரர் ராக்ஷசர் உயரறிவுடைய ஜீவர்கள், சுதந்திரர்கள் பிரம சைதன்னியம் காரிய ரூபத்தோடு கூடிய சுத்ததேகி கூடஸ்த சைதன்னியம் - காரிய காரண அரூபத்தோடு கூடிய பிரணவதேகி சர்வசாக்ஷி - காரண அரூபத்தோடு கூடிய ஞானதேகி
translation: Jeeva consciousness: cloud-space.
Ishvara consciousness: water-space.
Brahma consciousness: pot-space
Kutastha consciousness: tattva-space
Witness of all: great space

Jeeva consciousness: from the tiny mite up to the dull among human beings, dependent on others. Ishvara consciousness: asuras, rakshasas and jeevas of high knowledge, independent. Brahma consciousness: the pure-bodied one, joined with form as effect. Kutastha consciousness: the Pranava-bodied one, joined with effect, cause and the formless. Witness of all: the wisdom-bodied one, joined with cause and the formless.
commentary: Set out as a table, the scheme differs from the main passage in two details. The independent beings are now asuras and rakshasas, with no gods named. And the Pranava-bodied one is joined with the formless, where the main passage said form and formless together. The mite's name is spelled thambappuchi here.
The five kinds of consciousness as five spaces
1. Jeeva consciousness: cloud-space. All who depend on others, from the tiny mite up to the dull among human beings.
2. Ishvara consciousness: water-space. The independent: gods, asuras and souls of high knowledge.
3. Brahma consciousness: pot-space. The pure-bodied one, joined with form as effect.
4. Kutastha consciousness: tattva-space. The Pranava-bodied one, joined with effect-and-cause and the formless.
5. The witness of all: great space. The wisdom-bodied one, joined with cause and the formless.
The five are named in kevala Vedanta (note 64).

tamil: கடவுள் ஏகம் அனேகம் என்பதற்குப் பொருள்: சமயத்தில் சிவம் ஏகம், பிரமாதிக ளனேகம்; மதத்தில் பிரமம் ஏகம், ஜீவர்கள் அனேகம்; சாதாரணத்தில் கடவுள் ஏகம், பசுக்கள் அனேகம்; சுத்த சன்மார்க்கத்தில் தனிக்கடவுள் ஏகம், அவ்வருளால் சுத்தமாதி ஞான தேகம் வேறாகப் பெற்ற ஞானிகள் அனேகம் எனக் கொள்க.
translation: What "God is one and many" means. In religion, Sivam is one and Brahma and the rest are many. In the creeds, Brahman is one and the jeevas are many. In the common view, God is one and the bound souls are many. In Suddha Sanmarkkam, the one God alone is one, and the wise who by that grace have each gained the wisdom bodies, the pure body and the rest, are many. Take it so.
commentary: Every level of teaching agrees that God is one. They differ on who the many are, and Vallalar walks through four answers.

Samayam is religion, the level of worship and rites, and matham the creeds or schools of doctrine (see note 52). In religion the many are the lesser gods, Brahma and the others, under the one Sivam. In the creeds they are the jeevas, the individual souls, under the one Brahman. The common view makes them the pasu, the souls bound like cattle (see note 43).

In Suddha Sanmarkkam the many are the wise who have received, by God's grace, the bodies from the pure body up to the wisdom body (see note 8). The Tamil says they gain them "each separately". On this path those who attain stay many. They live, each in a body of grace, while God remains the one God alone, tanikkadavul, the God beside whom there is no other.

blocks.html: God, One and Many (கடவுள் ஏகம் அனேகம்)

tamil: கடவுள் ஏகம் அனேகம் என்பதற்குத் தாத்பரியம்: சமயத்தில் சிவம் ஏகம், பிரமாதிக ளனேகம். சமயாதீதத்தில் சொல்லிய பிரமம் முதல் சுத்தப் பிரமம் வரையிலும் ஏகம், அதைப் பெற்றவர்களனேகம். சாதாரண பாகத்தில் கடவுள் ஏகம், ஜீவர்கள் அனேகம். சுத்த சன்மார்க்கத்தில் கடவுள் ஏகம். கடவுளருளால் சுத்தமாதி மூன்று தேகங்களைப் பெற்ற ஞானிகஎனேகம்.
translation: The sense of "God is one and many": in religion, Sivam is one and Brahma and the rest are many. In what is beyond religion, what is spoken of, from Brahman up to pure Brahman, is one, and those who have gained it are many. In the common part, God is one and the jeevas are many. In Suddha Sanmarkkam, God is one, and the wise who by God's grace have gained the three bodies, the pure body and the others, are many.
commentary: In this shorter record the creeds are called "beyond religion", and their many are those who have reached Brahman. The common view counts jeevas where the main passage said bound souls. The three bodies are named outright.
God, one and many
On each row the large light is the one, and the small figures are the many.
1. In religion: Sivam is one; Brahma and the rest are many.
2. In the creeds: Brahman is one; the jeevas are many.
3. In the common view: God is one; the bound souls are many.
4. In Suddha Sanmarkkam: God alone is one; the wise who by His grace have gained the pure body and the other wisdom bodies are many.

sections.title: God as One and as Two

tamil: கடவுள் ஒன்றல இரண்டல ஒன்றுமிரண்டுமானார் என்பதற்குத் தாத்பரியம்: ஒன்றல - கடவுளானவர் ஒன்றாகிய ஞானதேகியும் அல்ல. இரண்டல - சுத்தப் பிரணவதேகியும் அல்ல. ஒன்றுமிரண்டுமானார் - கடவுளானவர் தன்னருளைப் பெற்ற சுத்த ஞானிக்கு ஞானதேகத்தையும் சுத்தப் பிரணவதேகத்தையுங் கொடுக்க முதற் கருவியாக இருக்கின்றார். இதை அனுபவத்தால் குருமுகத்தில் உணர்க.
translation: The sense of "God is not one, not two, and became one and two". Not one: God is not the wisdom-bodied one, who is one. Not two: nor is He the one with the pure Pranava body. Became one and two: God stands as the first instrument that gives the wisdom body and the pure Pranava body to the pure jnani who has gained His grace. Know this by experience, from the guru face to face.
commentary: "Not one, not two" is an old way of speaking about God and the soul. It refuses to say they are simply the same, and refuses to say they are simply apart. Vallalar reads the riddle through his bodies of grace (see note 8).

"One" is the wisdom body, in which the soul is as close to God as it can be. "Two" is the pure Pranava body, where some distinction remains. God is neither of these. He does not have such a body, as though He were one more attainer. He gives them. As the mudal karuvi, the first instrument, He is the one through whom the jnani, the one who knows, receives both. That is how God "became one and two".
The note ends by sending the reader past words. This must be known by anubhavam, experience (see note 7), and learned from a guru face to face.

tamil: சகலர், பிரளயாகலர், விஞ்ஞானகலர் ஆக 3. சகலர் இயற்கையாகிய ஆணவம், இயற்கையில் செயற்கையாகிய மாயை. செயற்கையாகிய காமியம் அல்லது கர்மம் இம்மூன்று முள்ளவர். பிரளயாகல இயற்கையாகிய ஆணவம், இயற்கையில் செயற்கையாகிய மாயை இவ்விரண்டு முள்ளவர். விஞ்ஞானகலர் இயற்கையாகிய ஆணவம் மாத்திரம் உள்ளவர். சகலர் ஜீவர்கள். பிரளயாகலர் கல்ப தேகிகள். விஞ்ஞானகலர் காலாதீதர்கள். சுத்தம் 9, அசுத்தம் 9, ஆக 18.
translation: Sakalar, pralayakalar and vijnanakalar, 3 in all. The sakalar have these three: anava, which is natural, maya, which is acquired within the natural, and kamya or karma, which is acquired. The pralayakalar have these two: anava, which is natural, and maya, which is acquired within the natural. The vijnanakalar have only anava, which is natural.
The sakalar are the jeevas. The pralayakalar are those whose bodies last a kalpa. The vijnanakalar are those beyond time. Pure 9, impure 9, 18 in all.
commentary: Saiva teaching sorts souls into three classes by how many of the three malas, the impurities, still bind them (see note 10). The sakalar carry all three. The pralayakalar carry two. Only one binds the vijnanakalar.

Each impurity has its place in the order. Anava is the soul's own darkness, there from beginningless time, so Vallalar calls it natural. Maya is the stuff of bodies and worlds (see note 3). It is acquired, though it comes "within the natural", fitted to the soul's darkness. Kamya means deeds done out of desire, and karma is deeds with their fruits. That one is plainly acquired. What comes last goes first, and anava, the root, is the last to go.

Vallalar then says who these classes are. The sakalar are the jeevas, ordinary embodied souls like us. The pralayakalar have bodies that last a whole kalpa, a cosmic age. The vijnanakalar are beyond time.
At the end comes a count of nine pure and nine impure that has nothing to attach to here. It matches the short record of note 68, where the gunas become eighteen in exactly this way.
The three kinds of souls
1. The sakalar, the jeevas: anava, maya and karma.
2. The pralayakalar, whose bodies last a kalpa: anava and maya.
3. The vijnanakalar, beyond time: anava alone.
4. Anava, which is natural. 5. Maya, acquired within the natural. 6. Karma (kamya), which is acquired.

tamil: தானாக நிற்றல் சத்துவகுணம், ராகத் துவேஷ சம்பந்தமுடையது ராஜசம், சோம்பலாதி ஜீவ இம்சைக் கிடனாவது தாமசம். ஆன்மாவின் செயற்கை ரஜோதமங்கள், இயற்கை சத்துவம். ஜனன மரண ஏது செயற்கையாலுண்டாம்; இயற்கையால் சிவானுபவம் பெறலாம். இதை விரிக்கில், ஒவ்வொன்றும் மும்மூன்றாகும், அனந்தமுமாம்.

சத்துவம் ராஜசம் தாமசம் தானாக நிற்றல் சத்துவம். இராகத் துவேஷாதிகளோடு கூடியது இராஜசம். ஜீவஹிம்சை செய்தல், சோம்பல், நித்திரை முதலியன தாமசம். ஆகையா லியற்கையாகிய சத்துவத்தோடு கூடிச் செயற்கையாகிய ராஜச தாமசத்தைச் சிறுகச் சிறுக நீக்க வேண்டியதில் சதா ஞாபகம் செய்யவேண்டியது.
translation: Standing as oneself is the quality of sattva. What is bound up with desire and aversion is rajas. What makes room for sloth and the rest, and for harm to living beings, is tamas. Rajas and tamas are acquired in the soul. Sattva is natural to it. The cause of birth and death comes from the acquired. Through the natural one can gain the experience of Siva. Spread out, each becomes three, and endless too.

Sattva, rajas, tamas. Standing as oneself is sattva. What goes with desire, aversion and the like is rajas. Harming living beings, sloth, sleep and the like are tamas. So, joined with the natural sattva, one must keep it always in mind to remove the acquired rajas and tamas little by little.
commentary: The gunas are the three qualities that Indian teaching finds in everything that acts. Sattva is clarity, rajas restless passion, tamas heaviness and darkness. Vallalar defines them in his own way.

Sattva is "standing as oneself", the soul resting in its own nature. Rajas is whatever is caught up in desire and aversion, the liking and disliking of note 61. Tamas is sloth and sleep, and it is also harm to living beings. Notice where he puts cruelty. It belongs with the dullest quality, the one furthest from the soul's nature.

The key pair is natural and acquired, iyarkai and seyarkai, the same pair note 10 used. Sattva is natural. Rajas and tamas are added on, and the acquired is what keeps birth and death turning. The natural opens the way to the experience of Siva.
The second record turns this into a practice. Rest in sattva, keep the aim always in mind, and wear away rajas and tamas little by little. Every refusal to harm a living being is part of that work.

tamil: சத்துவம், ராஜஸம், தாமசம் என்று குணங்கள் 3. ஒவ்வொன்றிலும் 3 சேர்ந்து 9 ஆயின. இந்த 9-ம் சுத்தம் அசுத்தம் என்னும் பேதத்தால் 18 ஆயின.
translation: The gunas are 3: sattva, rajas and tamas. With 3 joined in each, they became 9. By the division of pure and impure, these 9 became 18.
commentary: Here is the count that the main passage only hinted at, each guna spreading into three. It also explains the stray line "pure 9, impure 9, 18 in all" at the end of note 67.
The three gunas, nine and eighteen
1. Sattva: standing as oneself. It is natural to the soul.
2. Rajas: what is bound up with desire and aversion. It is acquired.
3. Tamas: sloth, sleep and harm to living beings. It is acquired.
4. With three joined in each, they became 9.
5. By the division of pure (filled) and impure (open), the 9 became 18.
Joined with the natural sattva, one removes the acquired rajas and tamas little by little.

tamil: சுத்த சன்மார்க்க லக்ஷிய அனுபவ விருப்ப முடையவர்களுக்கு நனவினும் மண்ணாசை, கனவினும் பெண்ணாசை, சுழுத்தியினும் பொன்னாசை முதலிய மூன்றுங் கூடாவாம்.
translation: Those who long for the experience of the goal of Suddha Sanmarkkam must not have these three: the desire for land even in waking, the desire for a woman even in dream, the desire for gold even in deep sleep.
commentary: Land, woman and gold, mannasai, pennasai and ponnasai, are the classic three desires of Tamil teaching on renunciation. The note speaks to the men who were listening. For any seeker the point is the same pull toward possession and pleasure.

What is new is where Vallalar tracks them. Each is tied to a state of mind: land to waking, woman to dream, gold to deep sleep. The word "even" carries the weight. Controlling desire while awake is the ordinary discipline. He asks that desire lose its pull even where no effort reaches, in dreams and in dreamless sleep. Desire that survives down there is vasanai, the impression left by the past (see note 31). His goal asks for its roots, too.
The three desires to be given up
