tamil: இந்தப் பவுதிக உடம்பிலிருக்கிற நீ யாரெனில்: நான் ஆன்மா, சிற்றணு வடிவன். ஷெ அணு கோடி சூரியப் பிரகாசமுடையது, லலாடஸ்தானமிருப்பிடம், கால்பங்கு பொன்மை முக்கால்பங்கு வெண்மை கலந்த வண்ணம். இப்படிப்பட்ட ஆன்மப் பிரகாசத்தை மறைக்க மாயா சத்திகளாகிய 7 திரைகளுண்டு. அவையாவன:
கறுப்புத் திரை மாயாசத்தி.
நீலத்திரை கிரியாசத்தி.
பச்சைத்திரை பராசத்தி.
சிவப்புத்திரை இச்சாசத்தி.
பொன்மைத்திரை ஞானசத்தி.
வெண்மைத்திரை ஆதிசத்தி.
கலப்புத்திரை சிற்சத்தி.*
translation: If it is asked, "Who are you, dwelling in this physical body?", the answer is: I am the soul, in the form of a minute atom. That atom has the light of ten million suns. Its seat is the forehead. Its color is a blend of one quarter gold and three quarters white. To hide such a light of the soul there are 7 screens, which are powers of maya. They are:
The black screen: the power of maya.
The blue screen: the power of action.
The green screen: the supreme power.
The red screen: the power of will.
The golden screen: the power of knowledge.
The white screen: the primal power.
The mixed screen: the power of consciousness.*
commentary: The note opens with the oldest question, "Who are you?", and answers it without hesitation. You are the anma, the soul. You are a sitranu, a minute atom, and its light is that of ten million suns. It sits in the forehead, and its color is a quarter gold and three quarters white. The body around it is bhautika, made of the elements.

Seven thirai, screens, hide that light from us. Each is a Sakti, a power, and each has its color. Black is Maya Sakti, blue Kriya Sakti, the power of action, and green Para Sakti, the supreme power. Red is Iccha Sakti, the power of will, gold Jnana Sakti, the power of knowledge, white Adi Sakti, the primal power, and the mixed screen Chit Sakti, the power of consciousness. Note 7 named most of these powers already. Here all seven are called powers of maya, because their work is to cover.

Vallalar returns to the seven screens in his Great Teaching, the Perupadesam, and in the Agaval lines that follow. The practical point is full of hope. A screen only hides, and the light behind all seven is untouched.

tamil: ச் கரைவின்மா மாயைக் கரும்பெருந் திரையால்
அரைசது மறைக்கும் அருட்பெருஞ் ஜோதி
பேருறு நீலப் பெருந்திரை அதனால்
ஆருயிர் மறைக்கும் அருட்பெருஞ் ஜோதி
பச்சைத் திரையால் பரவெளி அதனை
அச்சுற மறைக்கும் அருட்பெருஞ் ஜோதி
செம்மைத் திரையால் சித்துறு வெளியை
அம்மையின் மறைக்கும் அருட்பெருஞ் ஜோதி
பொன்மைத் திரையால் பொருளுறு வெளியை
அன்மையின் மறைக்கும் அருட்பெருஞ் ஜோதி
வெண்மைத் திரையால் மெய்ப்பதி வெளியை
அண்மையின் மறைக்கும் அருட்பெருஞ் ஜோதி
கலப்புத் திரையால் கருதனு பவங்களை
அலப்புற மறைக்கும் அருட்பெருஞ் ஜோதி
- திருஅருட்பா, அருட்பெருஞ்ஜோதி அகவல் 813-826
translation: With the great black screen of shoreless maya
Arut Perum Jothi hides the Sovereign.
With the vast and great blue screen
Arut Perum Jothi hides the precious soul.
With the green screen the supreme space
Arut Perum Jothi hides, so that awe arises.
With the red screen the space where consciousness dwells
Arut Perum Jothi hides in that very state.
With the golden screen the space where the Real dwells
Arut Perum Jothi hides, as if it were other.
With the white screen the space of the true Lord
Arut Perum Jothi hides, though it is near.
With the mixed screen the experiences one longs for
Arut Perum Jothi hides, so that the heart is troubled.
Thiru Arutpa, Arutperunjothi Agaval, lines 813-826.
commentary: Fourteen lines from the Arutperunjothi Agaval, Vallalar's long hymn to the Vast Grace-Light, and the source of the list above. Every couplet ends on the same name. Arut Perum Jothi is the One who draws each screen. The black hides the Sovereign, God Himself. The blue hides the soul. Green, red, gold and white hide four ever finer spaces, the supreme space, the space of consciousness, the space of the Real and the space of the true Lord. The mixed screen hides the very experiences the seeker longs for.

So the hiding is itself the work of grace. A screen drawn by Arut Perum Jothi is lifted by the same hand, and a few lines further on, beyond this extract, the Agaval shows the Light removing every screen and revealing the reign of truth.
The seven screens over the soul
1. The black screen: the power of maya. It hides the Sovereign.
2. The blue screen: the power of action. It hides the precious soul.
3. The green screen: the supreme power. It hides the supreme space.
4. The red screen: the power of will. It hides the space where consciousness dwells.
5. The golden screen: the power of knowledge. It hides the space where the Real dwells.
6. The white screen: the primal power. It hides the space of the true Lord.
7. The mixed screen: the power of consciousness. It hides the experiences one longs for.
8. The soul, an atom with the light of ten million suns, seated in the forehead, its color one quarter gold and three quarters white.

tamil: ரசவாதம் 7
ஸ்பரிசவாதம் - குரு சம்பந்தத்தால்
ரசவாதம் - ஓஷதி சம்பந்தத்தால்
தூமவாதம் - புகைவேதியால்
தாதுர்வாதம் - பஞ்சலோகங்களால்
வாக்குவாதம் - சொல்லால்
அக்ஷுவாதம் - பார்வையால்
சங்கல்பவாதம் - தியானத்தால் - செய்யப்படும்.
translation: Alchemy: 7
Sparisa vadam, by contact with the guru
Rasa vadam, by contact with herbs
Dhuma vadam, by transmuting smoke
Dhatur vadam, by the five metals
Vakku vadam, by the word
Akshu vadam, by the glance
Sankalpa vadam, by meditation. So they are done.
commentary: Rasavadam is alchemy, the art of turning one thing into another, most famously base metal into gold, and the Tamil Siddhas wrote much about it. Vallalar lists seven kinds. They run from outer means to inner ones: the touch of a guru, herbs, transmuting smoke and the five metals, then the spoken word, the glance and finally sankalpam, resolve held in meditation.

The first deserves a second look. Sparisam is touch. In note 3 the parisam, the touchstone said to turn base metal into gold by contact, stood beside the grace of the teacher that removes the soul's rust. A guru's touch that changes a disciple is alchemy in its truest sense.
Vallalar records these arts and leaves them there. In note 129 he places every such outer means on the lower path and tells the seeker of Suddha Sanmarkkam not to trust it.

tamil: மந்திரவாதம் - எழுத்துகள் சம்பந்தத்தால்
புரீஷவாதம் - மலமூத்திரத்தினால்
தூளனவாதம் - பாததூளிகை சம்பந்தத்தால்
வாயு பிரேரகவாதம் - சுவாச சம்பந்தத்தால்
தேவாங்கவாதம் - உபாசனையினால்
பிரவேச விசிரிம்பித வாதம் - பூத தாதுவால்
தந்திரவாதம் - நிரேதுவாக - செய்யப்படும்.
translation: Mantra vadam, by contact with letters
Purisha vadam, by stool and urine
Dhulana vadam, by contact with the dust of the feet
Vayu preraka vadam, by contact with the breath
Devanga vadam, by worship
Pravesa visrimbhita vadam, by the minerals of the elements
Tantra vadam, without cause. So they are done.
commentary: Uparasavadam means the lesser alchemies. There are seven more, worked through the letters of a mantra, through bodily wastes, through the dust of a holy one's feet, through the breath, through worship and through the minerals of the elements. The last, tantra vadam, works nirhetuvaka, without any cause one can name. The heading gives the list and nothing more, and the verdict of note 129 on outer means covers these as well.

tamil: நவநிலை என்பது அனுபவ மார்க்கம்.
நாதம்.
பரவிந்து
பரநாதம்
திக்கிராந்தம்
அதிக்கிராந்தம்
சம்மௌனம்
சுத்தம்
translation: The nine states are the path of experience.
Nada
Para Bindu
Para Nada
Thikkirantham
Athikkirantham
Sammaunam
Suddham
commentary: Navanilai, the nine states, are called anubhava margam, the path of experience. They are stages one passes through and knows by living them.

The print lists seven names here and an eighth, Atheetham, as a separate heading, so one name is missing. It is probably Bindu. Note 133 runs Bindu, Nada, Para Bindu and Para Nada in that order, and Nada here stands without its partner. Bindu and nada first appeared in note 1, the seed-point of light and the primal sound, whose shining in the sky is lightning and thunder. Para makes each of them "supreme".

The next two names are harder. Athikkirantham echoes the Sanskrit atikranta, "gone beyond", and thikkirantham may be "beyond the directions", though the note explains neither. Sammaunam is complete silence, suddham the pure, and atheetham, in the heading, the beyond.
ATHEETHAM, THE STATE BEYOND (அதீதம்)

tamil: குளிகை மணி ஒன்பதின் விவரம்: 1. பரம்பரமணி - அண்டத்தையும் அண்ட வஸ்துக்களையும் காட்டுவது. 2. பராபரமணி - பிண்டத்தையும் பிண்ட வஸ்துக்களையும் காட்டுவது.
3. அரும்பெறன்மணி - நினைத்ததை நினைத்தபடி அருளுவது.
4. ககனமாமணி - விண்ணுலக வஸ்துக்களை ஆட்டி வைக்கும்.
5. சரஒளிமணி - மண்ணுலகையும் மண்ணுலக வஸ்துக்களையும்
வைக்கும்.
6. கலைநிறைமணி - எல்லா வுலகத்தும் உலாவுதல்.
7. வித்தகமணி - சர, அசர வஸ்துக்களிடம் விளங்குவது.
8. சித்திசெய்மணி - மகாசித்திகளை நடத்துவது.
9. வளரொளிமணி - அழியாப் பெருவாழ்வு அளிப்பது.*
translation: The details of the nine kuligai gems: 1. Paramparamani: shows the cosmos and the things of the cosmos. 2. Paraparamani: shows the body and the things of the body.
3. Arumperal mani: grants what is thought, just as it is thought.
4. Kaganamamani: sets in motion the things of the heavenly worlds.
5. Saraoli mani: the earth and the things of the earth
it holds in place.
6. Kalainirai mani: moving through all worlds.
7. Vithaga mani: shines in moving and unmoving things.
8. Siddhisei mani: conducts the great siddhis.
9. Valaroli mani: grants the great life that never perishes.*
commentary: A kuligai is a pill or bead of the Siddhas, a hardened preparation said to give powers to whoever holds it. Mani is a gem. Here nine gem-pills are named with their powers, and the names come straight from the Agaval lines that follow, where every gem is a name of God.

Put into plain words, the names run like this: the gem supreme beyond the supreme and the gem both beyond and here (1 and 2), the rare gem hard to gain, the great gem of the sky, the gem of moving light, the gem full of the arts, the gem of mastery, the gem that works siddhis, and the gem of growing light. The first shows the cosmos with all it holds, the second the body with all it holds, in the old pairing of note 1.

Item 5 has lost a word in the print. It ends with vaikkum, "holds in place", and item 4 suggests the missing word is "sets in motion". The ninth gem gives the gift the whole close of the book is about, azhiyap peruvazhvu, the great life that never perishes.
The nine kuligai gems
1. Paramparamani: shows the cosmos and the things of the cosmos.
2. Paraparamani: shows the body and the things of the body.
3. Arumperal mani: grants what is thought, just as it is thought.
4. Kaganamamani: sets in motion the things of the heavenly worlds.
5. Saraoli mani: holds in place the earth and the things of the earth.
6. Kalainirai mani: moving through all worlds.
7. Vithaga mani: shines in moving and unmoving things.
8. Siddhisei mani: conducts the great siddhis.
9. Valaroli mani: grants the great life that never perishes.
The colors only tell the gems apart.

tamil: அண்டமும் அதன்மேல் அண்டமும் அவற்றுள
பண்டமும் காட்டிய பரம்பர மணியே
பிண்டமும் அதில்உறு பிண்டமும் அவற்றுள
பண்டமும் காட்டிய பராபர மணியே
நினைத்தவை நினைத்தவை நினைத்தாங் கெய்துற
அனைத்தையும் தரும்ஓர் அரும்பெறல் மணியே
விண்பதம் அனைத்தும் மேற்பத முழுவதும்
கண்பெற நடத்தும் ககனமா மணியே
பார்பதம் அனைத்தும் பகர்அடி முழுவதும்
சார்புற நடத்தும் சரஒளி மணியே
அண்டகோ டிகள்எலாம் அரைக்கணத் தேகிக்
கண்டுகொண் டிடஒளிர் கலைநிறை மணியே
சராசர உயிர்தொறும் சாற்றிய பொருள்தொறும்
விராயுள் விளங்கும் வித்தக மணியே
மூவரும் முனிவரும் முத்தரும் சித்தரும்
தேவரும் மதிக்கும் சித்திசெய் மணியே
தாழ்வெலாம் தவிர்த்துச் சகமிசை அழியா
வாழ்வெனக் களித்த வளர்ஒளி மணியே
- திருஅருட்பா, அருட்பெருஞ்ஜோதி அகவல் 1291-1308.
translation: The cosmos, the cosmos above it, and the things within them
You showed, O Paramparamani!
The body, the body within it, and the things within them
You showed, O Paraparamani!
So that whatever is thought, whatever is thought, is gained just as it is thought,
You give all things, O one Gem rare to gain!
All the heavenly stations and the whole of the stations above
You conduct in clear view, O great Gem of the sky!
All the earthly stations and the whole of the regions named below
You conduct, upholding them, O Gem of moving light!
So that all the crores of worlds may be passed through in half an instant
and beheld, You shine, O Gem full of the arts!
In every life, moving and unmoving, in every thing that is named,
You shine, mingled within, O Gem of mastery!
The Three, the sages, the freed, the Siddhas
and the gods honor You, O Gem that works siddhis!
Removing all my lowliness, an undying life in this world
You gave me, O Gem of growing light!
Thiru Arutpa, Arutperunjothi Agaval, lines 1291-1308.
commentary: In the Agaval each gem is Arut Perum Jothi, spoken to directly. The powers listed above as the properties of gem-pills are here the works of God. He shows the cosmos and the body, grants what is thought, moves the heavens and upholds the earth, carries the seer through countless worlds in half an instant, and shines from within every life and every named thing. The Three, Brahma, Vishnu and Rudra, honor Him along with sages, Siddhas and gods.

The last couplet changes voice. It is Vallalar's own testimony, in the first person. The Gem of growing light removed all his lowliness and gave him, here in this world, a life that does not perish. Sagamisai, "upon the world", is the word to notice. The deathless life he speaks of is lived in the world and in a body, and the remaining notes describe those bodies.
So the nine kuligai are finally one. Whatever power a Siddha's pill was said to hold belongs to the Light, and the Light gives it.

tamil: திரயோதச நிலைகள் யாவெனில்:
1. பூதநிலை 8. சுத்தமகாமாயாநிலை
2. கரணநிலை 9. சர்வமகாமாயாநிலை
3. பிரகிருதி நிலை 10. குண்டலிநிலை
4, மோகினிநிலை 11. பிரணவநிலை
5. அசுத்தமகாமாயாநிலை 12. பரிக்கிரகநிலை
6. அசுத்தமகாமாயாநிலை 13. திருவருள்நிலை
7. சுத்தமாயாநிலை
translation: What are the thirteen states?
1. The state of the elements, 8. The state of pure great maya
2. The state of the faculties, 9. The state of universal great maya
3. The state of primal nature, 10. The state of kundali
4. The state of mohini, 11. The state of Pranava
5. The state of impure great maya, 12. The state of parigraha
6. The state of impure great maya, 13. The state of divine grace
7. The state of pure maya
commentary: Thirayodasam is Sanskrit for thirteen. The print sets these states in two columns, one to seven on the left and eight to thirteen on the right, and they climb from the coarsest to the finest. First come the bhutas, the elements, then the karanams, the inner faculties of note 1, then prakriti, primal nature. Then come the layers of maya, the stuff of bodies and worlds. Mohini, the deluding one, is in Saiva usage a name for impure maya, and above it rise impure great maya, pure maya, pure great maya and universal great maya. Higher still are kundali, the coiled power, Pranava, the sound Om, and parigraha, which Saiva teaching names as the power of Siva that works upon pure maya. At the top is thiruvarul, divine grace.

The print gives "impure great maya" twice, at 5 and 6, so one of them was probably another name. Note 18 used the phrase "the end of the thirteen" for a different count of states, from the jeeva's waking up to the Guru states. Both counts end where grace begins.

tamil: ஆக 13. இதற்கதீதத்தில் சுத்த சிவநிலை. இதற்குச் சத்தி, ஆகாயம், நிலை, வெளி, பிரகாசம், அனுபவம், பதம், இடம் முதலிய பெயருள்ளன.

மேலும், வர்னமாகிய எழுத்தாலும், வண்ணமாகிய ரூபத்தாலும், தொழிலாகிய பெயராலும் அனந்தமாக விரியும். இவை யாவும் ராகமென்கிற திரை நீங்கினால் ஒருவாறு தோன்றும். மேலும் இவைகள் படிப்பால் அறியக்கூடாது. அறிவது எப்படி யெனில்: ஒழுக்கம் நிரம்பிக் கருணையே வடிவாக நிற்கும் விசார சங்கல்ப முண்டானால், நாம் தாழுங் குணம் வரும். அத்தருணத்தில் திருவருட்சத்தி பதிந்து அறிவு விளங்கும். ஆதலால், இடைவிடாது நன்முயற்சியில் பழகல் வேண்டும்.
translation: 13 in all. Beyond these is the state of pure Siva. It has names such as power, space, state, open space, radiance, experience, station and place.

Further, it spreads out endlessly by letter, which is sound, by form, which is color, and by name, which is function. All these appear in some measure if the screen called attachment is removed. Further, these cannot be known by study. How then are they known? If a resolve of inquiry arises that is full of right conduct and stands with compassion itself as its form, the quality of lowering ourselves will come. At that moment the power of divine grace settles in, and knowledge shines. So one must practice good effort without a break.
commentary: Beyond all thirteen lies suddha Siva nilai, the state of pure Siva. Vallalar gives it many names, power, space, state, open space, radiance, experience, station and place, and says it spreads without end through letter, form and name. Each word catches one side of something no single word holds.

He asks how it is known, and his answer begins with a refusal. It cannot be learned by study. What opens it is a screen lifted. Ragam, attachment, is that screen, and when it goes these states appear in some measure.

Then he gives the order of events, and it repays slow reading. First comes a vichara sankalpam, a resolve to inquire, full of ozhukkam, right conduct, and standing in the very form of compassion. From that comes humility, the quality of making ourselves low. At that moment thiruvarut sakti, the power of divine grace, settles in, and knowledge shines.

Compassion stands at the start of the sequence and grace at its end. The work in between is nanmuyarchi, good effort, kept up without a break, and note 3 has already said what good effort is. It is Jeevakarunyam, compassion for every living being. The way across all thirteen states is a compassionate life lived without interruption.
The thirteen states

1. The state of the elements. 2. Of the faculties. 3. Of primal nature. 4. Of mohini. 5. and 6. Of impure great maya (the list names it twice). 7. Of pure maya. 8. Of pure great maya. 9. Of universal great maya. 10. Of kundali. 11. Of Pranava. 12. Of parigraha. 13. Of divine grace.
14. Beyond these, the state of pure Siva, called power, space, state, open space, radiance, experience, station and place.
These are not known by study. They appear when the screen of attachment is removed and a resolve of inquiry arises, full of right conduct, with compassion itself as its form.

sections.title: The States of Experience in Jnana Yoga

tamil: ஆயிரத்தெட்டுக் கமல இதழ்
ஓங்காரபீடம்
குண்டலிவட்டம்
ஜோதிஸ்தம்பம்
translation: The lotus of a thousand and eight petals
The seat of Omkara
The circle of kundali
The pillar of light
commentary: The heading is padikamedai, the crystal platform, and under it come four places met on the way of jnana yoga, the yoga of wisdom. Yoga writings speak of a thousand-petalled lotus at the crown of the head, and Vallalar gives it a thousand and eight petals. The Omkara peetam is the seat of the sound Om. Kundali vattam is the circle of the coiled power, which he set among the thirteen states in note 125. Jothi sthambam is the pillar of light.
He offers only the names. Crystal lets light pass straight through, which may be why the heading calls these places a crystal platform. The next lines say how they are to be known.
The crystal platform
1. The lotus of a thousand and eight petals.
2. The seat of Omkara.
3. The circle of kundali.
4. The pillar of light.
Know these by experience. The note gives no order among them, so they stand side by side.

tamil: இவற்றை அனுபவத்தினாலறிக. இஃது நிராதார லக்ஷணம்.
translation: Know these by experience. This is the mark of the state without support.
commentary: Suththa nadanam, the pure dance, is the heading, and it recalls note 1, where the stirring of God's light within the soul's light is the dance and the one who moves is Nataraja. Of all these inner places Vallalar says only this, know them by experience. They are the marks of niradharam. The adharas are the supports, the centers in the body on which yoga rests the mind. Niradharam is the state that rests on none of them.

sections.title: The Places of Experience in Suddha Sanmarkkam

tamil: சுத்த சன்மார்க்கத்துக்கு அனுபவ ஸ்தானங்கள் கண்டத்துக்கு மேல்.
translation: For Suddha Sanmarkkam, the places of experience are above the throat.
commentary: One line, and it marks this path off from much of yoga practice. Many schools begin at the muladhara, the root center at the base of the body, and raise the power upward. Vallalar places the experiences of Suddha Sanmarkkam above the kandam, the throat. The notes have pointed there all along. God's light as cause sits between the brows in note 1. The soul's seat is the forehead in note 121. The pure nectars of note 120 rise from the tongue to the forehead.

tamil: சமாதிப் பழக்கம் பழக்கமல்ல. சகஜப் பழக்கமே பழக்கம்.
translation: The practice of samadhi is not the practice. The practice of the natural state alone is the practice.
commentary: Here Vallalar himself sets two practices side by side. Samadhi is the deep absorption of yoga, in which the senses close and the world falls away. It comes and goes, and one returns from it. Sahajam means "born with", the natural state. It is the state that stays, with the eyes open and the hands at work, while serving food or speaking with a neighbor.

He calls only the second a real pazhakkam, a practice, something grown into until it is simply how one lives. This fits the rest of the late notes. In note 125 grace settles on good effort kept up "without a break". A trance has breaks. A life lived in God's presence at every hour has none.

sections.title: The Undying Head, the Unburning Air, the Water That Does not Flow Away

tamil: சாகாத்தலை, வேகாக்கால், போகாப்புனல் என்பவற்றிற்குப்பொருள் யா தெனில்:- அடியில் வருவனேயாம். சாகாத்தலையென்பது ருத்திரபாகம், ருத்திரதத்துவம், வித்யாகலை, வஸ்து, அருளானந்தம், காரணாக்கினி, சிவாக்கினி. வேகாக்காலென்பது மகேசுவரபாகம், மகேசுவரதத்துவம், சாந்திகலை. ஆன்மா, அன்பு, காரணவாயு. போகாப்புனலென்பது சதாசிவபாகம், சதாசிவதத்துவம், பிரதிஷ்டாகலை, ஜீவன், இரக்கம், காரணோதகம். இவை மூன்றும் சாகாத கல்வியைத் தெரிவிக்கும். ஆத்ம தத்துவாதி சிவகரணம் 36, நிர்மல குருதுரியாதீதம் 7; ஆக நிலைகள் 43. இந்த 43 நிலைகளில் ஒவ்வொரு நிலைகளிலும் மேற்குறித்தவை உள. மேலும் இவை மூன்றும் பிண்டத்தில் நாலிடத்திலும் அண்டத்தில் நாலிடத்திலும் உள. அவைகள் பிண்டாண்ட ருத்திர சதாசிவ பேதம். சாகாக் கல்வியைக் குறித்த 43 நிலைகளில் முதல்நிலை அனுபவத்தைப் பெற்றுக் கொண்டவன் பிரமன். அவனது காலம் ஒரு கல்பம். இப்படி 43 நிலைகளையுமேறி அனுபவத்தைப் பெற்றவன் காலங்கடந்த காலாதீதன்.
translation: What is the meaning of the undying head, the unburning air and the water that does not flow away? It is what follows. The undying head is the Rudra portion, the Rudra tattva, Vidya kalai, the Substance, the bliss of grace, the causal fire, the fire of Siva. The unburning air is the Maheswara portion, the Maheswara tattva, Santhi kalai, the soul, love, the causal air. The water that does not flow away is the Sadasiva portion, the Sadasiva tattva, Prathishta kalai, the jeeva, pity, the causal water. These three make known the learning that does not die.

The 36, from the tattvas of the soul to the faculties of Siva, and the 7 of the stainless Guru state beyond the fourth: 43 states in all. In each of these 43 states the things named above are present. Further, these three are in four places in the body and in four places in the cosmos. They are the distinctions of Rudra and Sadasiva in the body and the cosmos.

Of the 43 states concerning the learning that does not die, the one who gained the experience of the first state is Brahma. His span is one kalpa. One who has climbed all 43 states in this way and gained their experience is the one beyond time, who has passed beyond time.
commentary: Sakathalai, vekakkal and pokappunal are three riddling phrases of the Siddha tradition: the head that does not die, the kal that does not burn, the water that does not go away. Kal means both leg and air, and Vallalar takes it as air. Many Siddha alchemists read the three as secret substances, salts or herbs to be prepared. Vallalar reads them as inner states.

He gives each a chain of correspondences. To Rudra belongs the undying head, which is fire, the bliss of grace and Vidya kalai. The unburning air belongs to Maheswara and is the soul, love and Santhi kalai. The water that does not flow away belongs to Sadasiva and is the jeeva, pity and Prathishta kalai, three of the five kalais named in Saiva teaching. Love and pity sit at the heart of the deathless.

These three open the sakakalvi, the learning that does not die, which notes 97 and 98 named. It is climbed in 43 states. Thirty-six are the tattvas of Saiva teaching, counted in note 55, from the soul's own tattvas up to those of Siva. Seven more belong to the Guru state beyond turiya, the fourth state, and note 18 named the Guru states.

His measure of the ladder is startling. Brahma the creator, whose lifespan is a whole kalpa, a cosmic age, has gained only the first rung. The one who climbs all 43 is kalatheethan, beyond time. The shorter record below gives the elements a little differently, space, air and fire, where this one gives fire, air and water.

tamil: மேற்குறித்த மூன்றும் பரமார்க்கமாகிய ஞானயோகக் காட்சியில் உண்டாகும் யோகானுபவங்களின் உண்மைப் பொருள். அபர மார்க்கத்தில் சிலர் உப்பு வகைகளின் பேதமென்றும் ஓஷதி பேதமென்றும் பூதபேத மென்றும் சொல்லுவது உபாயமார்க்கம். அக அனுபவமே உண்மை. உபாய வகையாகிய அபரமார்க்கம் தேக பூஷணாதி காமிய சித்தியைத் தரும். உண்மை, நீக்கமற்ற சொரூப ஞானத்தைத் தருமென்றறிக. மேற்படி உபாயங்களை ஒருவாறு தெரிவிப்பதும் சைவ சமயங்கள் தவிர வேறு எவ்வித சமயங்களிலுமில்லை. அப்படி யிருப்பதாகச் சொல்லியிருப்பதும் ஏகதேசமென்றறியவும். மேற்படி ஏகதேசங்கள்... மந்திரங்களிலும் மேற்படி மூன்றும் வழங்குகின்றபடியால், ஒன்பது மாற்றுக்கு மேற்பட்ட தங்கரேக்கில் பஞ்சாக்ஷரத்தையடைத்து விக்கிரகத்தின் அடியில் வைக்க, மகத்துவங்க ளுண்டாகும். மேலும் மேற்படி உயர்வுடைய தங்கத்தில் விக்கிரகஞ் செய்து வைத்து ஓஷதியாதி லவணங்களை அதற்குச் சேர்த்து வைத்தால், விசேஷ சித்தி விளங்கும். இஃது திரிசியக் காட்சி. சுத்த சன்மார்க்கத்திற்கு உபாய வகைகளான அபரமார்க்கக் காட்சி கூடாது. பரமார்க்கமாகிய அக அனுபவமே உண்மை. மேற்படி மூன்றையும் இலக்ஷியமாகவே கொள்க. உபாய வகையான வாச்சிய திரிசியக் காட்சிகள் பரோபகாரம். (?) ஆதலால், சாகாத்தலை வேகாக்கால் போகாப்புனலென்பவை இரண்டு புறத்திலுமுள. உபாய வகையை நம்புதல் கூடாது; உண்மையை நம்புதல் வேண்டும். இஃது ரகசியம்.
translation: These three are the true meaning of the yogic experiences that arise in the vision of jnana yoga, which is the higher path. On the lower path some say they are kinds of salt, kinds of herb, kinds of element. That is the path of means. Inner experience alone is the truth. The lower path, the kind that works by means, gives siddhis for desires, such as adorning the body. Know that the truth gives knowledge of one's own form, without separation.

Even the making known of these means in some measure is found in no religion other than the Saiva religions. Know that where they are said to be found elsewhere, it is only in part. Those parts... Since these three are present in mantras too, if the five-letter mantra is enclosed in gold foil finer than nine maattru and placed beneath an image, greatness arises. Further, if an image is made of gold of that high grade and herbs, salts and the like are joined to it, special siddhi shines forth. This is a visible sight.

For Suddha Sanmarkkam, the sight of the lower path, the kinds of means, is not fitting. The inner experience of the higher path alone is the truth. Take the three only in their inner sense. The literal and visible sights, the kinds of means, are help to others (?). So the undying head, the unburning air and the water that does not flow away are found on both sides. One must not trust the kind that is means. One must trust the truth. This is a secret.
commentary: Two paths read the same three phrases. Vallalar calls them para margam, the higher path, and apara margam, the lower. On the lower path the undying head, the unburning air and the water that does not flow away are taken as salts, herbs and elements, materials to be worked. He calls this upaya margam, the path of means. He grants that it works. It gives kamya siddhi, powers that serve desires, such as an adorned and splendid body. A gold foil finer than nine maattru, the old touchstone grades of gold, with the Panchakshara, the five-letter mantra, sealed in it and placed under a temple image, brings greatness to the shrine.

The higher path finds the same three as experiences within, seen in the vision of jnana yoga. What it gives is of another order, sorupa jnanam, knowledge of one's own true form, never separated from it.

Then comes a key for reading. Take the three as lakshya, in their indicated, inner sense. The vachya, the literal and visible sense, belongs to the means, and such outer sights, he adds with a query in the print, are a help to others.

His remark that only the Saiva religions hint at these means, and others only in part, concerns where this particular lore of means is recorded. In the next breath he tells the seeker of Suddha Sanmarkkam to set the means aside. Do not trust the means, he says. Trust the truth. He calls this a secret.

tamil: ஆங்கிரச ஸீ புரட்டாசி மாதம் 5ஆம் நாள்.
வேதாகமச் சிறப்பு

இந்து வேதாகமங்களில் மாத்திரந்தான் ஏமசித்தி ஞானசித்தி முதலிய சித்திகளைச் சொல்லியிருக்கின்றது. மற்ற எந்தச் சமயங்களிலும் மேற்படி சித்திகளையும் சாகாத கல்வியையும் சொல்லவில்லை. ஒருவேளை அப்படி யிருக்கிறதாகக் காணப்படுமாகில், அது இந்து வேதாகமங்களில் சொல்லியிருப்பதின் ஏகதேசங்களென்பது உண்மை.
translation: The year Angirasa, the 5th day of the month Purattasi.
The greatness of the Vedas and Agamas

Only the Hindu Vedas and Agamas speak of the siddhis such as the siddhi of gold and the siddhi of wisdom. No other religion speaks of these siddhis or of the learning that does not die. If perhaps they are seen to be there, the truth is that they are parts of what is said in the Hindu Vedas and Agamas.
commentary: A dated jotting. Angirasa is a year of the Tamil sixty-year cycle, and it fell in 1872-73. Purattasi is the month from mid-September to mid-October, so this note is dated two days after note 23.

The claim is narrow and exact. The Vedas and Agamas describe siddhis such as hema siddhi, the power of making gold, and jnana siddhi, the attainment of wisdom, and they speak of the learning that does not die. Vallalar says other religions do not describe these things, and that where something like them appears it is a part of what the Vedas and Agamas say. This is a remark about where one body of teaching is written down. It ranks no one's faith and asks no one to leave theirs.

It also sits beside a note that has just told the seeker not to trust outer means. Note 18 adds that experience above the Guru-turiya state, which the Vedas and Agamas mark only in some measure, is attainable in Suddha Sanmarkkam. Vallalar honors these scriptures as a record and keeps the path itself open to every human being.

tamil: பொன்னும் மகத்துவமும் ஒன்பது மாற்றுக்கு மேற்பட்ட பொன்னால் செய்த விக்கிரகங்கள் வைத்திருக்கும் தேவாலயங்களில் மகத்துவங்க ளுண்டாகும். மகத்துவத்தின் உயர்வு தாழ்வு பொன்னினது மாற்றுயர்வு தாழ்வாகவேயிருக்கும். மாற்றுயர்ந்த தங்கரேக்கில் பஞ்சாக்ஷரத்தை அடைத்து விக்கிரகத்தின் அடியில் வைக்க மகத்துவங்களுண்டாகும். இது ரகசியம்.
translation: Gold and greatness. In temples that keep images made of gold finer than nine maattru, greatness arises. The height or lowness of the greatness is just the height or lowness of the gold's fineness. If the five-letter mantra is enclosed in gold foil of high fineness and placed beneath the image, greatness arises. This is a secret.
commentary: Mahaththuvam, greatness, here means the felt power of a holy place. Vallalar ties it to the fineness of the gold in the image, measured in maattru. Finer gold, greater power. He calls this a secret, and the long record above has already placed it among the outer means, real in their working and not to be trusted by the seeker of Suddha Sanmarkkam.

blocks.html: The Undying Head, the Unburning Air, the Water That Does not Flow Away (சாகாத்தலை வேகாக்கால் போகாப்புனல்)

tamil: சாகாத்தலை ஆகாசம், வேகாக்கால் வாயு, போகாப்புனல் அக்கினி. சாகாத்தலையென்பது ருத்திரபாகம், ருத்திர தத்துவம். வேகாக்கால் என்பது மயேசுரபாகம் மயேசுரதத்துவம். போகாப்புனல் என்பது சதாசிவபாகம், சதாசிவதத்துவம். இம்மூன்றும் சாகாக்கல்வியைத் தெரிவிக்கின்றது. ஆத்மதத்துவாதி சிவகரணம் 36-ம் நிர்மல குரு துரியாதீதம் 7-ம் சேர்ந்து ஆனநிலை 43-ல் ஒவ் வொரு நிலையிலும் இவைகளுண்டு. மேலும் சாகாத்தலை, வேகாக்கால், போகாப்புனல் என்கிற தத்துவங்கள் பிண்டத்தில் 4 இடத்திலும், அண்டத்தில் 4 இடத்திலும் ஆக 8 இடத்திலும் உண்டு. இவைகள் பிண்டருத்திரர்கள் அண்டருத்திரர்கள் முதலிய ருத்திர மயேசுர சதாசிவ பேதமென்றறிக. சாகாக்கல்வியைக் குறித்த இந்த நாற்பத்துமூன்று நிலைகளில் முதனிலையின் அனுபவத்தைப் பெற்றுக் கொண்டவன் பிரமன். அவனுக்கு ஆயுசு 1 கற்பம். இப்படி 43 நிலைகளும் ஏறியனுபவத்தைப் பெற்றவன் காலங்கடந்தவன், காலரகிதன். சாகாத்தலை வேகாக்கால் போகாப்புனல் என்பவற்றிற்குப் பொருள் சிலர் உப்பு வகைகளின் பேதமென்று சொல்லுவது பிசகு. அவைகளினுண்மைப் பொருளை மேற்குறித்தபடி யோகக் காட்சிகளில் அனுபவிக்கலாம். ஆகையால் இவைகள் யோக அனுபவங்களே யென்று அறியவேண்டும்.
translation: The undying head is space, the unburning air is air, the water that does not flow away is fire. The undying head is the Rudra portion, the Rudra tattva. The unburning air is the Maheswara portion, the Maheswara tattva. The water that does not flow away is the Sadasiva portion, the Sadasiva tattva. These three make known the learning that does not die.

They are present in each of the 43 states formed by the 36, from the tattvas of the soul to the faculties of Siva, together with the 7 of the stainless Guru state beyond the fourth. Further, the tattvas called the undying head, the unburning air and the water that does not flow away are in 4 places in the body and 4 places in the cosmos, 8 places in all. Know that they are the distinctions of Rudra, Maheswara and Sadasiva, such as the Rudras of the body and the Rudras of the cosmos.

Of these forty-three states concerning the learning that does not die, the one who gained the experience of the first state is Brahma. His span of life is 1 kalpa. One who has climbed all 43 states in this way and gained their experience has passed beyond time and is free of time. Some say that the undying head, the unburning air and the water that does not flow away mean kinds of salt. That is an error. Their true meaning can be experienced in yogic visions, as said above. So know that these are yogic experiences only.
commentary: Most of the long record's words come back in this one. It differs on the elements, making the undying head space, the unburning air air and the never-flowing water fire. Its ending is the firmer of the two. To read the three as salts is pisaku, an error. They are yogic experiences only.
The undying head, the unburning air, the water that does not flow away
1. The undying head: space; the Rudra portion, the Rudra tattva; the causal fire, the fire of Siva.
2. The unburning air: air; the Maheswara portion; the soul, love, the causal air.
3. The water that does not flow away: fire; the Sadasiva portion; the jeeva, pity, the causal water.

These three make known the learning that does not die. They are in each of the 43 states, and in four places in the body and four in the cosmos. They are yogic experiences only; to take them as kinds of salt is an error.

tamil: கர்மசித்தி, யோகசித்தி, ஞானசித்தி எனச் சித்திவகை மூன்றாம். கர்மசித்தியாவது:-
அணிமா - துரும்பை மேருவாக்குகிறது
மகிமா - மேருவைத் துரும்பாக்குகிறது
கரிமா - மேருவை ஒன்றுமில்லாமல் செய்கிறது
லகிமா - ஒன்றுமில்லாத இடத்தில் அனேகங்களாகச் செய்கிறது பிராத்தி - வேண்டுவன அடைதல்
ஈசத்துவம் - குளிகை வல்லபத்தாலெங்கும் செல்லுகிறது
பிராகாமியம் - பரகாயப்பிரவேசம்
வசித்துவம் எழுவகைத் தோற்றமாகிய தேவமானுஷ்ய நரக மிருக பக்ஷி ஊர்வன விருக்ஷம் முதலியவற்றைத் தன்வசப்படுத்துகிறது.
தேகத்தைக் கல்பசித்தி செய்து கொள்ளுதல்; அபரமார்க்கி; சதாசிவாந்த அனுபவம்; சதாசிவகால வரை; பிரேதத்தை உயிர்ப்பித்தல்; சித்தி காலம் 3 3/4 நாழிகை முதல் 3 3/4 வருஷத்திற்குள்.
translation: Siddhi is of three kinds: karma siddhi, yoga siddhi and jnana siddhi. Karma siddhi is:
Anima: turning a straw into Mount Meru
Mahima: turning Meru into a straw
Garima: making Meru into nothing
Laghima: making many where there is nothing. Prapti: gaining what one wishes
Isatvam: going everywhere by the power of the kuligai
Prakamyam: entering another's body
Vasitvam: bringing under one's control the seven kinds of birth, gods, humans, beings of hell, animals, birds, crawling things, trees and the rest.

Making the body perfect by the elixir. One of the lower path. Experience up to the end of Sadasiva. Up to the time of Sadasiva. Reviving a corpse. Time of the siddhi: from 3 3/4 nazhigai to within 3 3/4 years.
commentary: The last notes climb through the fruits of the path, and this one sorts the siddhis, the attainments, into three grades: karma siddhi, gained through action and outer means, yoga siddhi, gained through yoga, and jnana siddhi, gained through wisdom.

Under karma siddhi come the eight classical powers, the ashta siddhi known across India's yoga traditions. Vallalar defines them in his own vivid way, with Mount Meru, the golden mountain at the center of the Puranic world, set against a single straw. In the usual lists anima is becoming minute and mahima becoming vast, and his pairing runs the other way. Garima makes the mountain vanish, laghima fills an empty place with many things, prapti gains what it wishes, isatvam goes everywhere by the power of a kuligai, the gem-pill of note 124, prakamyam enters another's body, and vasitvam commands the seven kinds of birth.

Then he places these powers. They come by making the body last through kalpa, the elixir, a word that also means a cosmic age. They belong to the apara margam, the lower path. Their experience reaches only to the end of Sadasiva, the highest of the five gods of note 133, and lasts only until Sadasiva's time. Even raising a corpse falls within this grade. The time to gain it runs from 3 3/4 nazhigai, an hour and a half, to under four years.
Mountains moved and the dead revived, and Vallalar still counts this the lowest of the three.

tamil: யோக சித்தி விவரம்:- 64 சித்திகளையும் தன் சுதந்தரத்தில் நடத்துகிறது; சங்கல்பகுளிகை; பிராணகல்பதேகி; பிரமகாலம்; பராபரமார்க்கி சித்திகாலம் 12 வருஷ முதல் 108 வருஷத்திற்குள் புதைத்த தேகத்தை நாசமடையாமுன் உயிர்ப்பித்தல்.
translation: Details of yoga siddhi: one conducts the 64 siddhis at one's own will. The kuligai of resolve. One whose body is perfected by the elixir of the breath. The time of Brahma. One of the higher and lower path. Time of the siddhi: from 12 years to within 108 years. Reviving a buried body before it perishes.
commentary: Yoga siddhi stands in the middle. Its holder commands the sixty-four siddhis freely. His kuligai is sankalpam itself, resolve, so he needs no pill. His body is a prana kalpa body, made lasting by mastery of the breath. He walks the parapara path, the higher and lower together, and can raise a body already buried before it decays. The training is long, from twelve years to a hundred and eight.

The print says this grade lasts "the time of Brahma". Beside the first grade, which lasts to Sadasiva's time, the figure looks out of order, unless Brahma here stands for Brahman. Note 131 gives these same marks to the Pranava body.

tamil: ஞானசித்திகளின் விவரம் - அறுபத்து நாலாயிரம் சத்திகளையும் தன் சுதந்திரத்தில் நடத்துகிறது. 647 கோடியாகிய*, 688 கோடி (?) பேதமாகிய மகாசித்திகளையும் தன்னிஷ்டம்போல் நடத்துகிறது; காலம் கடந்தது; அடிநிலை முடிநிலை சுத்தகர்ம, சுத்தயோக, சுத்தஞான சித்திவல்லபங்களைத் தன் சுதந்தரத்தால் நடத்துகிறது. ் ஆடுறு சித்திகள் அறுபத்து நான்கெழு
translation: Details of the jnana siddhis: one conducts all sixty-four thousand powers at one's own will. One conducts as one wishes the great siddhis of 647 crore*, 688 crore (?) kinds. Beyond time. By one's own freedom one conducts the powers of the siddhis of pure karma, pure yoga and pure jnana, from the lowest state to the highest. "The siddhis that dance forth, sixty-four, and seven
commentary: Jnana siddhi alone is kalam kadanthathu, beyond time. Its holder moves sixty-four thousand powers at will, and the great siddhis in their crores. The pure forms of all three grades, of action, of yoga and of wisdom, from the lowest state to the highest, come under his freedom.

The numbers in the print are puzzling, and the editor has marked them. "647 crore" may be the Agaval line quoted at the end, arupaththu nangu ezhu kodi, "sixty-four, and seven crores", run together into one figure. That line of verse begins here and runs on into the next line of the print.
What matters is the rank. In note 131 the third body, the body of wisdom, carries the same marks, every power, complete freedom, beyond time.
The three kinds of siddhi

1. Karma siddhi: the eight powers such as anima and mahima; the body made perfect by the elixir; the lower path; experience up to Sadasiva; reviving a corpse. Its time: from three and three-quarter nazhigai to within three and three-quarter years.

2. Yoga siddhi: the 64 siddhis at one's will; the body perfected by the elixir of the breath; the higher and lower path; reviving a buried body before it perishes. Its time: from 12 years to within 108 years.
3. Jnana siddhi: all sixty-four thousand powers at one's will; beyond time; by one's own freedom one conducts the siddhis of pure karma, pure yoga and pure jnana.

blocks.html: Crores, Shining: O True Substance Who Delights! (கோடியும் விளங்கக் குலவுமெய்ப்பொருளே)

tamil: - அருட்பெருஞ்ஜோதி அகவல் 911-2
translation: Thiru Arutpa, Arutperunjothi Agaval, lines 911-912.
commentary: The couplet, read whole: "O true Substance, who delights in making shine the sixty-four siddhis that dance forth and the seven crores!" Every siddhi in this note, from moving Meru to the powers beyond time, shines by Arut Perum Jothi. The one who attains holds them as gifts of the Light.

sections.title: The Pure Body and the Two Bodies Beyond It

tamil: சுத்தமாதி மூன்று தேக விவரம்: சுவர்ணதேகம், பிரணவதேகம், ஞானதேகம்.
12 வயது பருவம்
நரை, திரை, பிணி,
மூப்பு, மலம், ஜலம்,
வியர்வை, ஆகாரம்,
நித்திரை, தாகம்,
சாயை முதலியன
இல்லாமை
ரோம வளர்ச்சி
தாழ்ச்சி இல்லாமை
கர்மசித்தி
கல்பதேகி
அபரமார்க்கி
5 முதல் 8 வயது
தேகம் தோற்றும்,
பிடிபடாது.
சர்வ சித்தி
பிராண கல்பதேகி
பர அபர மார்க்கம்

சுவர்ண தேகம் பிரணவ தேகம் ஞானதேகம் காரிய ரூபம் காரிய காரண ரூபம் காரண ரூபம் பரதேகம் பரம்பர தேகம் எங்கும் பூரண பர உணர்ச்சி பரம்பர உணர்ச்சி வியாபகம் பர அறிவு பரம்பர அறிவு பராபர அறிவு பரத்துவம் பரம்பர தத்துவம் பராபர தத்துவம் பொன் வண்ணம் 16 முதல் 108 வரையில் அளவு கடந்த மாற்று அபரஞ்சி மாற்று மாற்று, உரைபடாதது
சப்த மயதரிசனம்
உருவம் தோற்றியும்
தோற்றாமலும் இருக்கும்
translation: Details of the three bodies beginning with the pure body: the golden body, the Pranava body, the body of wisdom.
The age of 12 years
Gray hair, wrinkles, disease,
old age, stool, urine,
sweat, food,
sleep, thirst,
shadow and the like:
none of these
Growth of hair
no decline
Karma siddhi
One with an elixir body
One of the lower path
The age of 5 to 8 years
The body appears
but cannot be grasped.
All siddhis
One whose body is perfected by the elixir of the breath
The higher and lower path

The golden body, the Pranava body, the body of wisdom. The form of effect, the form of effect and cause, the form of cause. The para body, the parampara body, complete everywhere. Para feeling, parampara feeling, pervading. Para knowledge, parampara knowledge, parapara knowledge. Paratvam, the parampara tattva, the parapara tattva. The color of gold, from 16 to 108 maattru, fineness beyond measure. The fineness of aparanji, fineness upon fineness, that which no touchstone can test.
A vision made of sound
The form both appears
and does not appear.
commentary: This note was printed as a chart with three columns, one for each body, and the printed text has run its rows together. Read across, they give a portrait of the three bodies of attainment. Note 8 spoke of a different three, the body of action, the Pranava body and the body of wisdom. Here the first is the suddha deham, the pure body, which the note also calls the suvarna deham, the golden body.

The golden body stays twelve years old. Gray hair, wrinkles, disease and age do not touch it. It passes no stool or urine, does not sweat, needs no food or sleep, feels no thirst and casts no shadow. Its hair neither grows nor falls, or, as the line can also be read, its hair grows and it knows no decline. It belongs to karma siddhi, to the one whose body is made lasting by kalpa, and to the lower path.
The pranava deham looks five to eight years old. It can be seen and cannot be grasped. It holds all siddhis, it is made lasting by the breath, and it belongs to the higher and lower path together.
The jnana deham, the body of wisdom, is a vision made of sabda, sound. Its form appears and does not appear. The heading below adds its last marks, every great power, complete freedom, beyond time.

The long middle row sets the three side by side, effect, effect and cause, and cause, and so on up the scale of para, the supreme. Their gold grows finer from 16 to 108 maattru, then beyond measure, and at last to aparanji, the finest gold, which no touchstone can assay. The three grades of siddhi in note 130 match these bodies column by column. Vallalar teaches them as real fruits of the path, and in the verse of note 124 he speaks of the undying life as given to him.

tamil: சுதந்தரம்
காலாதீதன்
translation: All freedom
One beyond time
commentary: The heading and these two lines finish the third column of the chart. The body of wisdom has sarva maha sakti, every great power, and sarva suthantharam, complete freedom. Its bearer is kalatheethan, beyond time, the word note 129 used for the one who climbs all 43 states.
The three bodies beginning with the pure body
1. The golden body (pure body): the form of effect; it looks twelve years old; no gray hair, wrinkles, disease, old age, stool, urine, sweat, food, sleep, thirst or shadow.
2. The Pranava body: the form of effect and cause; it looks five to eight years old; the body appears but cannot be grasped.
3. The body of wisdom: the form of cause; a vision made of sound; the form both appears and does not appear; complete everywhere, all freedom, beyond time.

tamil: சுவர்ண தேகிகள் ஆயுள். ஒரு மாற்றுள்ள சுவர்ண தேகிகள் வயசு - நாலு லக்ஷத்து முப்பத்தீராயிரம்.
இரண்டு மாற்றுள்ள சுவர்ண தேகிகள் வயசு - எட்டு லக்ஷத்து அறுபத்து நாலாயிரம்.
மூன்று மாற்றுள்ள சுவர்ண தேகிகள் வயசு - பன்னிரண்டு லக்ஷத்து தொண்ணூற்று ஆறாயிரம்.
நான்கு மாற்றுள்ள சுவர்ண தேகிகள் வயசு - பதினேழு லக்ஷத்து இருபத் தெட்டாயிரம்.
ஐந்து மாற்றுள்ள சுவர்ண தேகிகள் வயசு - நாற்பத்து மூன்று லக்ஷத்து இருபதாயிரம்.
ஐந்து பூதங்களின் பேதம் பன்னிரண்டு லக்ஷத்து இரண்டாயிரத்து எண்ணூ ற்று ஐம்பது கோடியாய் இருக்கின்றது.
translation: The lifespan of those with golden bodies. Those with a golden body of one maattru: age 432,000.
Those with a golden body of two maattru: age 864,000.
Those with a golden body of three maattru: age 1,296,000.
Those with a golden body of four maattru: age 1,728,000.
Those with a golden body of five maattru: age 4,320,000.
The kinds of the five elements are twelve lakh two thousand eight hundred and fifty crore.
commentary: Each grade of fineness in the golden body adds to its span. Maattru is the old measure of the purity of gold, tested on a touchstone, and here it measures the purity of a body.

The numbers come from the old reckoning of time. In the Puranic count of the four ages, 432,000 years is the Kali age, 864,000 the Dvapara, 1,296,000 the Treta and 1,728,000 the Krita, and 4,320,000 is their sum, the great age. So a golden body of one maattru lives through a Kali age, and one of five maattru lives through all four. In note 133 the same five figures become the ages of the five gods.

Long as these spans are, each has an end. Only the body of wisdom in note 131 is beyond time. The last line turns to the elements and counts their kinds at twelve lakh two thousand eight hundred and fifty crore. A lakh is a hundred thousand and a crore ten million, so the figure is 12,028,500,000,000.
The lifespans of the golden-bodied
The bars are drawn to scale.
1. A golden body of one maattru: 432,000 years.
2. Of two maattru: 864,000.
3. Of three maattru: 1,296,000.
4. Of four maattru: 1,728,000.
5. Of five maattru: 4,320,000.
Note 133 gives the same figures for Brahma (five maattru) up to Sadasiva (nine maattru).

sections.title: The Experiences of Anu Paksha and Sambhu Paksha

tamil: ஐந்து மாற்றுள்ள சுவர்ணதேகி பிரமன் வயசு - நாலு லக்ஷத்து முப்பத்தீராயிரம்.
ஆறு மாற்றுள்ள சுவர்ணதேகி விண்டு வயசு - எட்டு லக்ஷத்து அறுபத்து நாலாயிரம்.
ஏழு மாற்றுள்ள சுவர்ணதேகி ருத்திரன் வயசு - பன்னிரண்டு லக்ஷத்துத் தொண்ணூற்று ஆறாயிரம்.
எட்டு மாற்றுள்ள சுவர்ணதேகி மயேசுரன் வயசு - பதினேழு லக்ஷத்து இருபத்தெட்டாயிரம்.
ஒன்பது மாற்றுள்ள சுவர்ணதேகி சதாசிவன் வயசு - நாற்பத்து மூன்று லக்ஷத்து இருபதினாயிரம்.
இவர் அணுபக்ஷத்தார்.
translation: Brahma, with a golden body of five maattru: age 432,000.
Vishnu, with a golden body of six maattru: age 864,000.
Rudra, with a golden body of seven maattru: age 1,296,000.
Maheswara, with a golden body of eight maattru: age 1,728,000.
Sadasiva, with a golden body of nine maattru: age 4,320,000.
These belong to the anu paksha.
commentary: Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra, Maheswara and Sadasiva each receive a golden body of a certain fineness and a lifespan to match. The spans are the five figures of note 132, from 432,000 to 4,320,000 years. The grades of gold do not line up with that note, where five maattru already gave the longest life. Here five maattru gives Brahma the shortest, so the two lists seem to use different scales.

The last line names the order these gods belong to. Paksha means side or class, and note 9 named five classes of creation, among them anu and sambhu. In Saiva teaching the anu paksha are souls, anus, who have risen to hold the offices of these gods for a time, while in the sambhu paksha Siva Himself works through the same offices. So the five of this passage are great souls with a span. They are not the Supreme, and the deathless life Vallalar describes lies beyond even their ages.

tamil: அணுபச்ஷத்தில் நாற்பத்து மூவாயிரத்து இருநூறு லக்ஷங்கோடி விந்து சத்தியின் அளவு; அளவிறந்த கோடி நாதத்தின் அளவு.
அணுபக்ஷத்தில் பரவிந்து சுத்தமாயையைக் கடந்தது; பரநாதம் சுத்தமகாமாயையைக் கடந்தது.
translation: In the anu paksha, the measure of the power of Bindu is forty-three thousand two hundred lakh crore. The measure of Nada is crores beyond measure.
In the anu paksha, Para Bindu has passed beyond pure maya. Para Nada has passed beyond pure great maya.
commentary: Above the five gods of the anu paksha stand four more powers, the names that open the nine states of note 123, Bindu and Nada, then Para Bindu and Para Nada. The measure of Bindu's power is forty-three thousand two hundred lakh crore, which is 432 followed by fourteen zeros, the same 432 that runs through the ages of note 132. Nada's measure is past counting. Their supreme forms have crossed beyond pure maya and pure great maya, the finest layers of the thirteen states in note 125.

tamil: சம்பு பக்ஷத்தில் பிரமன், விண்டு, ருத்திரன், மயேசுரன், சதாசிவன், விந்து, நாதம், பரவிந்து, பரநாதம் என்பவற்றில்:
பிரமன், விண்டு - சுத்த மகா மாயையைக் கடந்த ஞான அனுபவ பேதம். ருத்திரன் - சித் அனுபவம்
மயேசுரன் - ஆனந்த அனுபவம்
சதாசிவன் - சத் அனுபவம்
விந்து - சிதானந்த அனுபவம்
நாதம் - சதானந்த அனுபவம்
பரவிந்து - சச்சிதானந்த அனுபவம்
பரநாதம் - சிவானுபவம். இவை ஒருவாறு.
உபதேசக் குறிப்புகள் முற்றிற்று.
translation: In the sambhu paksha, of Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra, Maheswara, Sadasiva, Bindu, Nada, Para Bindu and Para Nada:
Brahma and Vishnu: the distinct experiences of knowledge that have passed beyond pure great maya. Rudra: the experience of consciousness.
Maheswara: the experience of bliss.
Sadasiva: the experience of being.
Bindu: the experience of consciousness and bliss.
Nada: the experience of being and bliss.
Para Bindu: the experience of being, consciousness and bliss.
Para Nada: the experience of Siva. These, in some measure.
Here end the Notes of Teachings.
commentary: The same nine names return, now on the sambhu paksha, the side where Siva Himself works. Here they stop being persons with spans and become grades of experience. Brahma and Vishnu are experiences of knowledge beyond pure great maya. Rudra is chit, consciousness, Maheswara ananda, bliss, and Sadasiva sat, being. Bindu joins consciousness and bliss, and Nada joins being and bliss. Para Bindu holds all three together, sat-chit-ananda, the being, knowledge and bliss that note 49 found in the very name Sivam. Para Nada is Sivanubhavam, the experience of Siva.
Vallalar adds two words, ivai oruvaru, "these, in some measure". He has drawn a map, and he says so. The rest is known as note 126 said all these states are known, by experience.

He has also said where that experience begins. In note 125 the way to the state of pure Siva starts from a resolve of inquiry that stands in the form of compassion, and grace settles on the one who keeps up good effort without a break. Note 105 calls Jeevakarunyam the first step to liberation. The book opened with God's light in the four rings of body and cosmos, and it closes on the experience of Siva, reached through the door Vallalar names everywhere, compassion for every living being.

Observance; thirteen are named in note 103 as blocking compassion.
The teacher.
What is acquired and had a beginning, as the soul's fall is.
Non-duality, where the two cease and one remains; in note 44 the stepless way of the Veda, which is experience.
The clay lamp bowl, the body.
The inner, the first of the four places; in the body the soul, in the cosmos fire.
The inner-outer place; in the body the jeeva, in the cosmos the sun.
Egoism, one face of Brahma.
The egotist.
Space.
The twelve saints of the Vaishnava faith.
The new-moon night, when moon and sun are joined.
The nectar air, which sustains and fills the cosmos from first dawn to sunrise.
Nectar, the drink that keeps death away.
Without beginning.
What is natural and without beginning, as anava is.
Not other, not foreign; how the paths of religion stand to Suddha Sanmarkkam.
The soul's innate darkness, the first of the three impurities; beginningless.
The great world of the cosmos, translated "the cosmos".
A year of the Tamil sixty-year cycle, 1872 to 1873.
The soul, the inner place, which knows the truth of a thing.
The gain of the soul, reached by the way with steps or the way without (note 44).
The oneness that comes from knowing every soul as one's own kin. The kinship of all souls (note 91).
The kinship of souls.
The feeling or awareness of the soul, one of the man's three.
The inner faculties: mind, intellect, memory and ego.
End; the final teaching of a school, as in Vedanta.
Atom; in the space of the soul the atoms are the souls.
Experience, which Vallalar sets against common reasoning.
Atoms, the souls; Brahma, Vishnu and Rudra were souls who did tapas.
Close, steady inner attention, contemplation; in note 52 contemplation of the tattvas.
A daily observance.
Lower knowledge, the learning of books and the world.
The finest gold, which no touchstone can assay.
The water tattva; Narayana presides over it (note 35) and the four Vedas came from its four qualities (note 42).
The six inner foes, lust, anger, greed, delusion, pride and envy.
The shining of knowledge.
One firmly established.
Grace.
The power of grace, beginningless in God.
The open space of grace.
The first red glow before sunrise.
The Vast Grace-Light, Vallalar's name for God, the Reality of Suddha Sanmarkkam.
The Pranava of grace; Vallalar's name for the vowel i in the letter si (note 49).
Craving; with infatuation, the two daughters the moon favored (note 29).
The Master.
The bodiless voice, heard from no speaker (note 75).
The eight classical powers, anima to vasitvam.
The beyond, where the seen is lost as well as the seer (note 81).
Desire; Ganapati in note 29, the demon Padumasura in note 31.
The intermediate aeon, one day of Brahma.
A state of consciousness; three, waking, dream and deep sleep (note 70).
The increase of the span of life.
The great life that never perishes.
The outer cosmic sphere beyond it.
A substance reduced to ash by fire, the last stage of the preparation.
Elemental; the minerals, poisons and herbs of Siddha medicine, and the body, read by Vallalar as "that which holds fire inside" (note 59).
Difference and non-difference (note 73).
Without difference, as equals.
Mastery over enjoyments, the fruit of meditating facing east.
An element, the root of the word bhautikam (note 59).
Seed; the letter si holds five (note 49).
The seed-point of light, whose shining in the cosmos is lightning; in note 14 the nectar part of the seed.
Knowledge of Brahman, which gains the golden body.
The great cosmic sphere.
The opening at the crown of the head.
Intellect.
The fine fire in the heart's white sac, Rudra's form.
Consciousness, in five grades from jeeva consciousness to the witness of all (note 64).
The old name for people pushed to the lowest place in the caste order; the moon's curse in the Purana is chandalatvam, the state of a chandala (note 29).
Temple service and ritual worship, the first two stages of Saiva practice.
A red calcined powder of Siddha medicine, made from iron and other metals.
The Hall of Consciousness; another name for the soul's light.
Purity of mind, the fruit of meditating facing north.
The crust on a wick, Vallalar's word for impure semen.
Ten million.
The form of compassion; to become it, cleared of impurity, is to become Sivam (note 51).
Compassion; the compassion of the Supreme Cause keeps the body alive.
The perfection of the body.
Celestials; those whose very form is compassion. A name of Thiruvalluvar, author of the Kural.
Righteousness; Vallalar defines it as compassion, kindness and grace.
A bodily constituent; the body has seven.
Initiation; read by Vallalar as the removal of impurity (note 82).
Defect; Vallalar defines it as darkness, not-knowing, ignorance.
Sight; the soul, jeeva and mind each have their own (note 62).
A foul smell, and a bad inner tendency.
"The end of twelve", a point yoga places above the crown of the head.
Duality; in note 44 the stepped way of the Agama, where worshipper and God are still two.
Garuda, Vishnu's eagle mount; read syllable by syllable as water, blackness and whiteness (note 36).
The Vedic mantra of twenty-four syllables; read as the three bodies to be crossed and as the grip on compassion and inquiry (note 55).
The three qualities; Siva's trident.
A height within the fourth state, the place of the experience of samarasa.
A touch of the hand used as a remedy.
The horse-headed form of Vishnu; read as "the one whose neck is the vital breath" (note 37).
The attainment of gold, the power to make gold (note 52).
The power of will; Virabhadra in the head (note 40).
The left; here Sakti, the soul's nature, which is grace.
The left, lunar breath current.
Place; Tamil grammar's word for a grammatical person (note 73).
Giving to those in need.
The householder, one who lives in a home with a family.
Mercy, owed to all eighty-four lakh kinds of birth.
"These, in some measure.".
The sacrificer, the soul among the eight forms of Siva; here the air or life in the woman's four.
A conjuror's trick; Vallalar's word for the claim that grace comes from an image.
"Conquered salt", salt purified and fixed for use in food.
The individual life, the inner-outer layer, which knows the use of a thing.
The jeeva's awareness of itself as a separate self, which says "I" and "mine"; Daksha (notes 29, 30).
The faults of living beings, which the mind must not search out.
The effort of the jeeva, a person's own striving (note 93).
The rule as it holds among jeevas, the ladder of servant, son, friend and self.
Compassion for all living beings; the good effort that removes the rust of the inner eclipse.
One freed while living, the witness of the mind (note 78).
The individual self; the particular jeeva in the throat, which dies.
Jeeva-hood, the jeeva's separateness, lost through worship (note 44).
Help given to living beings, which disliking blocks (note 61).
The body of wisdom.
The Hall of Wisdom; here the light of the soul.
One perfected in wisdom, witness in every hair (note 78).
The attainment of wisdom.
A creation of wisdom; the return of the dead (note 86).
One of true wisdom; only pure jnanis who have conquered maya write without error.
Causal heat, the fire held inside every elemental thing (note 59).
Cause; a different word from karanam, the faculty.
The end-and-head lock, a figure of Tamil grammar in which words trade places.
The hard-hearted, who have no compassion.
The hard-hearted one; set against Siva's great grace (note 50).
Siva's mountain; in note 16 a range of stations below the throat, in note 17 a white sac in the heart.
Foot, and also air; Vallalar reads Siva's foot as the vital breath.
A ray or portion of a light's power; also a tiny measure of time (note 9).
Learning of the arts, knowledge gathered from books (note 93).
Beyond time.
The first stage of the preparation in note 23; exact sense left to an expert.
One beyond time.
The siddha who completed the elixir and, unseen, moves the world through the Kali age.
Verdigris on copper, the image of the eclipsed jeeva.
A cosmic age.
The change of aeon, read as the dawning of experiential wisdom in the body.
Deeds done out of desire, the acquired impurity, karma (note 67).
Powers that serve desires.
The throat, above which the experiences of Suddha Sanmarkkam lie.
The Tamil Purana of Murugan and the war against Surapadma (note 31).
The faculty, chiefly the mind, which weighs name, form, qualities and faults.
Effect; God's light as effect shows in the eight places.
Deeds and their fruits, one of the three impurities.
The body of action.
Compassion.
Sight or vision; four kinds, of the senses, the faculties, the jeeva and the soul.
The soul alone in its darkness before embodiment; said of the moon.
Killing, the taking of any life, the gravest of the five sins (note 74).
Not killing, the first mark of sattva.
Death, a name of Yama; Vallalar's word for anger.
The field in which the seed rests.
Unclear here; a zinc preparation of some kind (note 32).
A word for the subtle source of the worlds; Vallalar defines it as primal nature (note 57).
A renunciate who stays within the family.
A Siddha pill or bead said to give powers.
The coiled power.
The changeless one, "standing like an anvil"; in note 64 the Pranava-bodied grade of consciousness (notes 63, 64).
Pit oil, drawn by heating a substance in a pot buried in the ground.

Gain; love is the gain of Jeevakarunyam.
A trace; the deities' power is a trace of God's.
A grade of the fineness of gold.

The great aeon, the whole life of Brahma.
The highest of the twenty-five doers of the five functions.

To set aside or decline; pure bindu and pure Sivam set aside both lower and higher.
The way of delusion.
The body of delusion, the body as confused understanding sees it.
A festival sparkler.
A small unit of measure.
The stuff from which bodies and worlds are made; one of the three impurities.

The path of the friend, another record's name for the companion's path.
Infatuation; the lion-faced brother of Surapadma (note 31), a favored daughter of the moon (note 29).

Silent bliss.

The chaff-flower plant.

The dance of justice.
The state that rests on none of the bodily supports.

Stainlessness.
